1	"""Secret resolution abstraction.
2	
3	Three backends are supported, picked from `settings.secret_store`:
4	
5	- **EnvSecretStore** — reads secrets from env vars prefixed `KV_SECRET_`.
6	  Local dev only — convenient when running against `docker-compose` without
7	  an Azure tenant. Name normalisation: `snowflake-uat-finance` →
8	  env var `KV_SECRET_SNOWFLAKE_UAT_FINANCE`. **Per-process**: a secret written
9	  via `set` is only visible to the writing process (#86).
10	
11	- **RedisSecretStore** — reads/writes secrets in Redis (already in the dev
12	  stack). **Dev/test only** and **plaintext** — but, unlike EnvSecretStore, a
13	  secret `set` by the API process is visible to the Celery worker, so
14	  connection-driven worker runs can resolve a credential the API just wrote
15	  (#86). Not for production (no encryption) — production uses Key Vault.
16	
17	- **AzureKeyVaultStore** — reads from Azure Key Vault via
18	  `azure-identity` (DefaultAzureCredential) + `azure-keyvault-secrets`.
19	  Production / staging. Real vault provisioning + tenant config land in
20	  Week 7 (deployment hardening); the code path is wired now so callers
21	  can take a dependency on `SecretStore` without waiting.
22	
23	The Azure SDK and the redis client are **lazy-imported** so deployments that
24	don't use them don't pay the import cost.
25	"""

28	
29	import os
30	import threading
31	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final, Protocol, runtime_checkable
32	
33	import redis

36	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger

39	    from azure.keyvault.secrets import SecretClient
40	
41	log = get_logger(__name__)
42	
43	ENV_PREFIX: Final = "KV_SECRET_"
44	_AKV_MODE: Final = "azure_key_vault"
45	_REDIS_MODE: Final = "redis"
46	# Namespace for secret keys in the shared dev Redis (keeps them clear of Celery's
47	# own keys on the same instance).
48	_REDIS_KEY_PREFIX: Final = "dataq:secret:"

50	
51	class SecretNotFoundError(Exception):
52	    """Raised when the requested secret is missing or unreadable."""
53	
54	
55	class SecretWriteError(Exception):
56	    """Raised when a secret cannot be written to the backing store."""
57	
58	
59	@runtime_checkable
60	class SecretStore(Protocol):
61	    def get(self, name: str) -> str: ...
62	
63	    def set(self, name: str, value: str) -> None: ...
64	
65	
66	def _env_key(name: str) -> str:
67	    return f"{ENV_PREFIX}{name.upper().replace('-', '_')}"
68	
69	
70	class EnvSecretStore:
71	    """Resolves secrets from `KV_SECRET_*` env vars. Local dev only."""
72	
73	    def get(self, name: str) -> str:
74	        key = _env_key(name)
75	        value = os.environ.get(key)
76	        if value is None:
77	            raise SecretNotFoundError(f"Env secret {key!r} not set (mapped from name={name!r})")
78	        return value
79	
80	    def set(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
81	        """Write into the process env. Dev only — NOT persisted across restarts.
82	
83	        Lets connection-CRUD exercise the write-through path locally without an
84	        Azure tenant. Production uses AzureKeyVaultStore, which persists.
85	        """
86	        os.environ[_env_key(name)] = value
87	
88	
89	class AzureKeyVaultStore:
90	    """Resolves secrets from Azure Key Vault via DefaultAzureCredential."""
91	
92	    def __init__(self, vault_url: str) -> None:
93	        self._vault_url = vault_url
94	        self._client: SecretClient | None = None
95	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
96	
97	    def _client_lazy(self) -> SecretClient:
98	        if self._client is not None:
99	            return self._client
100	        with self._lock:
101	            if self._client is None:
102	                from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
103	                from azure.keyvault.secrets import SecretClient
104	
105	                self._client = SecretClient(
106	                    vault_url=self._vault_url,
107	                    credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
108	                )
109	            return self._client
110	
111	    def get(self, name: str) -> str:
112	        try:
113	            secret = self._client_lazy().get_secret(name)
114	        except Exception as exc:
115	            raise SecretNotFoundError(
116	                f"Key Vault secret {name!r} at {self._vault_url}: {exc}"
117	            ) from exc
118	        value = secret.value
119	        if value is None:
120	            raise SecretNotFoundError(f"Key Vault secret {name!r} has no value")
121	        return str(value)
122	
123	    def set(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
124	        try:
125	            self._client_lazy().set_secret(name, value)
126	        except Exception as exc:
127	            raise SecretWriteError(
128	                f"Key Vault secret {name!r} at {self._vault_url}: {exc}"
129	            ) from exc
130	
131	
132	class RedisSecretStore:
133	    """Resolves secrets from Redis — dev/test only, plaintext, shared across processes.
134	
135	    The point (vs `EnvSecretStore`): Redis is shared, so a secret `set` by the API
136	    process is visible to the Celery worker, which is what connection-driven worker
137	    runs need (#86). Values are stored in **plaintext** — never use in production;
138	    production uses `AzureKeyVaultStore`. The redis client is lazy-built.
139	    """
140	
141	    def __init__(self, redis_url: str, *, key_prefix: str = _REDIS_KEY_PREFIX) -> None:
142	        self._url = redis_url
143	        self._key_prefix = key_prefix
144	        self._client: redis.Redis[str] | None = None
145	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
146	
147	    def _key(self, name: str) -> str:
148	        return f"{self._key_prefix}{name}"
149	
150	    def _client_lazy(self) -> redis.Redis[str]:
151	        if self._client is not None:
152	            return self._client
153	        with self._lock:
154	            if self._client is None:
155	                self._client = redis.Redis.from_url(self._url, decode_responses=True)
156	            return self._client
157	
158	    def get(self, name: str) -> str:
159	        try:
160	            value = self._client_lazy().get(self._key(name))
161	        except Exception as exc:
162	            raise SecretNotFoundError(f"Redis secret {name!r}: {exc}") from exc
163	        if value is None:
164	            raise SecretNotFoundError(f"Redis secret {name!r} not set")
165	        return str(value)
166	
167	    def set(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
168	        try:
169	            self._client_lazy().set(self._key(name), value)
170	        except Exception as exc:
171	            raise SecretWriteError(f"Redis secret {name!r}: {exc}") from exc
172	
173	
174	_store_singleton: SecretStore | None = None
175	_store_lock = threading.Lock()
176	
177	
178	def _build_store(settings: Settings) -> SecretStore:
179	    if settings.secret_store == _AKV_MODE:
180	        if not settings.azure_key_vault_url:
181	            raise RuntimeError(f"secret_store={_AKV_MODE!r} requires AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL")
182	        return AzureKeyVaultStore(settings.azure_key_vault_url)
183	    if settings.secret_store == _REDIS_MODE:
184	        return RedisSecretStore(settings.redis_url)
185	    return EnvSecretStore()
186	
187	
188	def get_secret_store() -> SecretStore:
189	    """Return the configured store (cached after first call)."""
190	    global _store_singleton
191	    if _store_singleton is not None:
192	        return _store_singleton
193	    with _store_lock:
194	        if _store_singleton is None:
195	            settings = get_settings()
196	            _store_singleton = _build_store(settings)
197	            log.info("secret_store_initialized", backend=settings.secret_store)
198	        return _store_singleton
199	
200	
201	def reset_secret_store_cache() -> None:
202	    """Test-only: clear the cached store so the next call rebuilds it."""
203	    global _store_singleton
204	    with _store_lock:
205	        _store_singleton = None
206

         store.set("conn-snowflake-dev-finance", "p@ss")
 
 
+class _StubCredential:
+    """Stands in for DefaultAzureCredential — records that it was constructed."""
+
+
+class _StubSecretClient:
+    """Stands in for SecretClient — records ctor args and serves get/set."""
+
+    instances: ClassVar[list["_StubSecretClient"]] = []
+
+    def __init__(self, *, vault_url: str, credential: object) -> None:
+        self.vault_url = vault_url
+        self.credential = credential
+        self.set_calls: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+        _StubSecretClient.instances.append(self)
+
+    def get_secret(self, name: str) -> SimpleNamespace:
+        return SimpleNamespace(value=f"value-of-{name}")
+
+    def set_secret(self, name: str, value: str) -> None:
+        self.set_calls.append((name, value))
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()
+def stub_azure_sdk(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> type[_StubSecretClient]:
+    """Patch the real SDK classes so `_client_lazy`'s import branch runs for real.
+
+    Unlike the tests above (which monkeypatch `_client_lazy` itself and so skip
+    the branch entirely), these patch `azure.identity.DefaultAzureCredential` and
+    `azure.keyvault.secrets.SecretClient` at module level — the in-function
+    `from azure... import ...` then resolves to the stubs, exercising the whole
+    lazy-construction path without any network. Discharges WEEK7 A4 (the 0%-cov
+    tail of #169).
+    """
+    _StubSecretClient.instances = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr("azure.identity.DefaultAzureCredential", _StubCredential)
+    monkeypatch.setattr("azure.keyvault.secrets.SecretClient", _StubSecretClient)
+    return _StubSecretClient
+
+
+def test_akv_client_lazy_constructs_sdk_client_with_vault_url_and_credential(
+    stub_azure_sdk: type[_StubSecretClient],
+) -> None:
+    store = AzureKeyVaultStore("https://example.vault.azure.net/")
+    assert store.get("snowflake-uat-finance") == "value-of-snowflake-uat-finance"
+    (client,) = stub_azure_sdk.instances
+    assert client.vault_url == "https://example.vault.azure.net/"
+    assert isinstance(client.credential, _StubCredential)
+
+
+def test_akv_client_lazy_caches_client_across_calls(
+    stub_azure_sdk: type[_StubSecretClient],
+) -> None:
+    store = AzureKeyVaultStore("https://example.vault.azure.net/")
+    first = store._client_lazy()
+    second = store._client_lazy()
+    assert first is second
+    assert len(stub_azure_sdk.instances) == 1
+
+
+def test_akv_store_set_reaches_sdk_through_lazy_branch(
+    stub_azure_sdk: type[_StubSecretClient],
+) -> None:
+    store = AzureKeyVaultStore("https://example.vault.azure.net/")
+    store.set("conn-snowflake-dev-finance", "p@ss")
+    (client,) = stub_azure_sdk.instances
+    assert client.set_calls == [("conn-snowflake-dev-finance", "p@ss")]
+

109	async def request_id_middleware(
110	    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
111	) -> Response:
112	    incoming = request.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)
113	    rid = incoming if incoming and _REQUEST_ID_RE.match(incoming) else uuid.uuid4().hex
114	    token = request_id_var.set(rid)
115	    # Path only — never request.url (it carries the query string, e.g. the ADF
116	    # webhook ?token=<secret>, ADR 0006 / #494). client host kept for audit.
117	    client = request.client.host if request.client else None
118	    start = time.perf_counter()
119	    try:
120	        response = await call_next(request)
121	    except Exception:
122	        elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)
123	        _log.exception(
124	            "request_failed",
125	            method=request.method,
126	            path=request.url.path,
127	            client=client,
128	            duration_ms=elapsed_ms,
129	        )
130	        request_id_var.reset(token)
131	        raise
132	    elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)
133	    _log.info(
134	        "request",
135	        method=request.method,
136	        path=request.url.path,
137	        client=client,
138	        status=response.status_code,
139	        duration_ms=elapsed_ms,
140	    )
141	    request_id_var.reset(token)
142	    response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
143	    return response

62	def _redact_pii(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:
63	    def walk(value: Any) -> Any:

66	        if isinstance(value, list):

68	        if isinstance(value, str):

76	def _add_request_id(_logger: Any, _name: str, event_dict: EventDict) -> EventDict:
77	    rid = request_id_var.get()
78	    if rid is not None:
79	        event_dict["request_id"] = rid
80	    return event_dict
81	
82	
83	def configure_logging() -> None:
84	    settings = get_settings()
85	    level = getattr(logging, settings.log_level)
86	
87	    shared_processors: list[Processor] = [
88	        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
89	        _add_request_id,
90	        structlog.processors.add_log_level,
91	        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
92	        _redact_pii,
93	    ]
94	
95	    # Bridge stdlib logging (uvicorn.access, uvicorn.error, etc.) through the
96	    # same processor chain so every line out of the app is JSON with a
97	    # request_id when available. Without this the uvicorn access log emits
98	    # human-readable text that App Insights can't correlate (#50).
99	    formatter = structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter(
100	        foreign_pre_chain=shared_processors,
101	        processors=[
102	            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.remove_processors_meta,
103	            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,
104	            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),
105	        ],
106	    )
107	
108	    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
109	    handler.setFormatter(formatter)
110	    root = logging.getLogger()
111	    root.handlers = [handler]
112	    root.setLevel(level)
113	
114	    # Detach uvicorn's pre-configured handlers; let logs propagate to root so
115	    # they hit the structlog ProcessorFormatter above.
116	    for name in ("uvicorn", "uvicorn.error"):
117	        uvicorn_logger = logging.getLogger(name)
118	        uvicorn_logger.handlers = []
119	        uvicorn_logger.propagate = True
120	
121	    # uvicorn.access is SILENCED, not propagated: its access line includes the raw
122	    # query string (get_path_with_query_string), so it would log the ADF webhook
123	    # `?token=<secret>` (ADR 0006) to stdout AND straight to App Insights (#494).
124	    # The request middleware (main.py) emits a structured, path-only access log
125	    # (method/path/status/duration/client/request_id) for every request that reaches
126	    # the app — so app-level access logging is unaffected; only server-layer-only
127	    # lines (e.g. malformed requests rejected before ASGI dispatch) go unlogged, an
128	    # accepted tradeoff for not leaking the secret.
129	    access_logger = logging.getLogger("uvicorn.access")
130	    access_logger.handlers = []
131	    access_logger.propagate = False
132	
133	    conn = settings.applicationinsights_connection_string
134	    if conn:
135	        from opencensus.ext.azure.log_exporter import AzureLogHandler
136	
137	        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)
138	
139	        # opencensus-ext-azure (unmaintained, not tested on Python 3.13 — ADR 0017)
140	        # overrides createLock() to set `self.lock = None` (it does its own
141	        # queue-based thread-safety). That was fine on older Python, but 3.13's
142	        # logging.Handler.handle() does `with self.lock` with no None-check, so the
143	        # first emitted record crashes app startup. Assigning the lock once isn't
144	        # enough: Celery's embedded beat (`worker -B`) re-initialises logging in
145	        # its forked process and calls createLock() AGAIN, re-nulling the lock and
146	        # killing beat on its first log line — so every periodic task (orchestration
147	        # polling, scheduled dispatch, gap recovery) silently stops (#405, a #393
148	        # recurrence). Replace createLock with an idempotent version that only ever
149	        # CREATES a missing lock and never nulls or swaps an existing one — so no
150	        # caller can re-null it, and a live lock is preserved rather than replaced
151	        # (avoids losing mutual exclusion if a re-init ever raced an in-flight
152	        # emit). (#393 — proper fix: migrate to azure-monitor-opentelemetry;
153	        # opencensus is EOL.)
154	        def _ensure_handler_lock() -> None:
155	            if getattr(ai_handler, "lock", None) is None:
156	                ai_handler.lock = threading.RLock()
157	
158	        ai_handler.createLock = _ensure_handler_lock
159	        ai_handler.createLock()
160	        ai_handler.setLevel(level)
161	        # Use the SAME ProcessorFormatter as stdout so records sent to App Insights
162	        # also pass through `_redact_pii` (incl. the secret-string scrubber). Without
163	        # a formatter, AzureLogHandler ships the raw record message, so a foreign
164	        # (non-structlog) record carrying a secret in its message would reach App
165	        # Insights un-redacted (#494). App-level structlog records are already
166	        # redacted in the wrapper chain; this closes the foreign-record path too.
167	        ai_handler.setFormatter(formatter)
168	        root.addHandler(ai_handler)
169	
170	    structlog.configure(
171	        processors=[
172	            *shared_processors,
173	            structlog.processors.dict_tracebacks,
174	            structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.wrap_for_formatter,
175	        ],
176	        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),
177	        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),
178	        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
179	    )
180	
181	
182	def get_logger(name: str | None = None) -> structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger:
183	    logger: structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger = structlog.get_logger(name)
184	    return logger
185

1	"""Celery application for DataQ's async execution backbone.
2	
3	GX suite runs are dispatched from FastAPI and executed here so the request
4	thread returns immediately (run created as ``queued``, worker drives it to
5	``running`` → ``succeeded``/``failed``).
6	
7	The CLAUDE.md observability rule requires ``request_id`` correlation to flow
8	FastAPI → Celery → GX. We carry it on the task message headers: the caller
9	injects the active request_id on publish, and the worker restores it into the
10	same ``request_id_var`` ContextVar the structlog processor chain reads from, so
11	worker log lines correlate with the request that triggered them.
12	"""
13	
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	from celery import Celery
17	from celery.signals import (
18	    beat_init,
19	    before_task_publish,
20	    setup_logging,
21	    task_postrun,
22	    task_prerun,
23	)
24	
25	from backend.app.core.config import get_settings
26	from backend.app.core.logging import configure_logging, get_logger, request_id_var
27	
28	# Message-header key carrying the originating request_id across the broker.
29	REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "request_id"
30	# Attribute on task.request where prerun stashes the ContextVar reset handle
31	# for postrun. Deliberately avoids the word "token" so it isn't mistaken for a
32	# secret by Bandit / Ruff (B105 / S105).
33	_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR = "_dataq_request_id_reset"
34	
35	
36	def create_celery_app() -> Celery:
37	    settings = get_settings()
38	    app = Celery(
39	        "dataq",
40	        broker=settings.redis_url,
41	        backend=settings.redis_url,
42	    )
43	    app.conf.update(
44	        task_serializer="json",
45	        result_serializer="json",
46	        accept_content=["json"],
47	        timezone="UTC",
48	        enable_utc=True,
49	        # Surface a 'started' state so the run-status read-back can distinguish
50	        # queued from running without waiting for completion.
51	        task_track_started=True,
52	        # Celery-beat schedule. The orchestration polling fallback (#171) runs
53	        # every 10 min as the success channel for runs that produced no webhook;
54	        # the task looks back further than the interval so nothing slips the gap.
55	        # Beat runs embedded in the dev worker (`worker -B`); prod uses a separate
56	        # beat process.
57	        # Gap recovery (B2) sweeps a wider 1-hour window every 30 min (plus once
58	        # on beat startup, via the beat_init signal below) to re-ingest runs
59	        # missed while the system was down — idempotent with the 10-min poll.
60	        beat_schedule={
61	            "poll-orchestration-runs": {
62	                "task": "poll_orchestration_runs",
63	                "schedule": 600.0,  # 10 minutes
64	            },
65	            "recover-orchestration-gaps": {
66	                "task": "recover_orchestration_gaps",
67	                "schedule": 1800.0,  # 30 minutes
68	            },
69	            # Scheduled suite runs (A7): tick every minute, fire schedules whose
70	            # precomputed next_run_at has passed. Minute granularity matches the
71	            # finest standard cron resolution; the task is a cheap indexed scan
72	            # when nothing is due.
73	            "dispatch-due-schedules": {
74	                "task": "dispatch_due_schedules",
75	                "schedule": 60.0,  # 1 minute
76	            },
77	            # Result retention sweep: once a day, scrub `sample_failures` (the only
78	            # potentially-PII result column) from results past the configured
79	            # retention window. Keeps the row + `metric_value` so dashboard trends
80	            # survive (ADR 0012); this is PII minimisation, not a history delete.
81	            "purge-sample-failures": {
82	                "task": "purge_sample_failures",
83	                "schedule": 86400.0,  # 24 hours
84	            },
85	            # Stuck-run reaper (#309): every 10 min, fail runs orphaned in a
86	            # non-terminal state past `stuck_run_threshold_minutes` (a run committed
87	            # `queued` before `send_task`, or left `running` by a dead worker). The
88	            # detection threshold (default 60 min) far exceeds the 10-min cadence, so
89	            # the sweep interval only bounds detection latency, not false reaps.
90	            "reap-stuck-runs": {
91	                "task": "reap_stuck_runs",
92	                "schedule": 600.0,  # 10 minutes
93	            },
94	        },
95	    )
96	    # Register task modules on worker boot (looks for backend.app.worker.tasks).
97	    app.autodiscover_tasks(["backend.app.worker"])

104	@setup_logging.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
105	def _configure_celery_logging(**_kwargs: Any) -> None:
106	    """Disable Celery's default logging and route worker logs through structlog.
107	
108	    Connecting any receiver to ``setup_logging`` tells Celery not to configure
109	    logging itself, so our JSON + PII-redacting processor chain stays in force
110	    inside the worker exactly as it is in the API.
111	    """
112	    configure_logging()
113	
114	
115	@before_task_publish.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
116	def _inject_request_id(headers: dict[str, Any] | None = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
117	    """Caller side (FastAPI): stamp the active request_id onto task headers."""
118	    if headers is None:
119	        return
120	    rid = request_id_var.get()
121	    if rid is not None:
122	        headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
123	
124	
125	@task_prerun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
126	def _restore_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
127	    """Worker side: restore request_id from the message into the ContextVar.
128	
129	    Custom headers added in ``before_task_publish`` are exposed as attributes on
130	    ``task.request`` under the protocol-v2 message format. We stash the reset
131	    token on ``task.request`` so ``task_postrun`` can restore the *prior* value
132	    rather than blindly clearing — under ``task_always_eager`` these signals run
133	    in the caller's context, so a blanket reset would drop the request_id for
134	    the rest of the request handler.
135	    """
136	    rid = getattr(task.request, REQUEST_ID_HEADER, None) if task is not None else None
137	    if rid and task is not None:
138	        token = request_id_var.set(rid)
139	        setattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, token)
140	
141	
142	@task_postrun.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
143	def _clear_request_id(task: Any = None, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
144	    """Worker side: restore the ContextVar to its pre-task value.
145	
146	    Only resets when ``task_prerun`` actually set it (token present), mirroring
147	    the ``reset(token)`` pattern used by ``request_id_middleware`` in main.py.
148	    """
149	    token = getattr(task.request, _REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR, None) if task is not None else None
150	    if token is not None:
151	        request_id_var.reset(token)
152	
153	
154	@beat_init.connect  # type: ignore[untyped-decorator]  # celery signal .connect is unannotated
155	def _recover_gaps_on_beat_start(**_kwargs: Any) -> None:
156	    """When the beat scheduler starts, kick a one-off gap recovery (B2).
157	
158	    Tied to ``beat_init`` (one beat process per deployment) rather than worker
159	    boot, so it fires **once** per restart instead of once per worker — no
160	    thundering herd of identical sweeps on a multi-worker deploy. Catches runs
161	    that completed while the system was down; the 30-min beat alone would leave
162	    that window unswept until its first tick. Enqueued by name (decoupled from
163	    the task module) to the broker so a ready worker runs it. Best-effort: a
164	    broker hiccup at startup must not crash beat (the schedule recovers shortly).
165	    """
166	    try:
167	        celery_app.send_task("recover_orchestration_gaps")
168	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive; startup must not fail on broker
169	        get_logger(__name__).exception("gap_recovery_startup_dispatch_failed")

{

  "content": "\"\"\"Request/task span instrumentation (WEEK7 A3 — App Insights spans).\n\nOTel-neutral core (ADR 0010): the OpenTelemetry SDK + FastAPI/Celery\ninstrumentations are vendor-neutral; Azure Monitor is one *exporter* behind\nthe seam (swap the exporter per cloud, nothing else changes). Everything is\ngated on ``settings.applicationinsights_connection_string`` — unset ⇒ a\ncomplete no-op, matching ``configure_logging()``'s AzureLogHandler gate.\n\nDeliberately the **exporter-only** package (`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-\nexporter`), NOT the `azure-monitor-opentelemetry` distro: the distro\nauto-configures the logging pipeline and would collide with the hardened\nstructlog + opencensus ``AzureLogHandler`` chain in ``logging.py``\n(#393/#405 Py3.13 lock fixes). Migrating the *log* pipeline opencensus→OTel\nis tracked separately; this module owns spans only.\n\nAll OTel/Azure imports are lazy (repo convention, see ``secrets.py``) so\ndeployments without App Insights never pay the import cost.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final\n\nfrom backend.app.core.config import get_settings\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nif TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from fastapi import FastAPI\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n# URLs whose server spans are never recorded (comma-separated regexes, the\n# opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi `excluded_urls` format): /healthz is\n# probe noise, and the orchestration webhook receivers carry a secret in the\n# query string (`?token=<secret>`, ADR 0006 / #494) which must never land in\n# span attributes such as `url.full`.\nEXCLUDED_URLS: Final = \"healthz,api/v1/orchestration/events/.*\"\n\n_provider: TracerProvider | None = None\n\n\ndef configure_tracing(service_name: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Install a TracerProvider exporting to App Insights, or no-op.\n\n    Idempotent per process (the global tracer provider can only be set once);\n    safe to call from both the API lifespan and the Celery worker-process-init\n    signal.\n    \"\"\"\n    global _provider\n    if _provider is not None:\n        return\n    conn = get_settings().applicationinsights_connection_string\n    if not conn:\n        return\n\n    from azure.monitor.opentelemetry.exporter import AzureMonitorTraceExporter\n    from opentelemetry import trace\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor\n\n    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({\"service.name\": service_name}))\n    provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(AzureMonitorTraceExporter(connection_string=conn)))\n    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)\n    _provider = provider\n    log.info(\"tracing_configured\", service_name=service_name)\n\n\ndef instrument_fastapi(app: FastAPI) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit a server span per request (minus EXCLUDED_URLS). No-op when tracing is off.\"\"\"\n    if _provider is None:\n        return\n    from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor\n\n    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(\n        app, tracer_provider=_provider, excluded_urls=EXCLUDED_URLS\n    )\n\n\ndef instrument_celery() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit a span per Celery task run. No-op when tracing is off.\"\"\"\n    if _provider is None:\n        return\n    from opentelemetry.instrumentation.celery import CeleryInstrumentor\n\n    CeleryInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=_provider)\n"
}

                class ExceptionHandlerMiddleware:

                error_middleware = ServerErrorMiddleware(

Migrating the *log* pipeline opencensus→OTel\nis tracked in #524; this module owns spans only.\n\nAll OTel/Azure imports are lazy (repo convention, see ``secrets.py``) so\ndeployments without App Insights never pay the import cost.\n\nCall-ordering constraint (learned the hard way in review): FastAPI\ninstrumentation patches ``app.build_middleware_stack``, and Starlette builds\nthe middleware stack on the FIRST ASGI call — which is the *lifespan scope\nitself*. So ``instrument_fastapi`` MUST run at module scope (before the app\nserves anything), never from inside the lifespan handler, or it silently\ninstruments nothing. ``backend/tests/core/test_tracing.py`` pins this with a\nregression test against the real ``backend.app.main`` wiring.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Final\n\nfrom backend.app.core.config import get_settings\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nif TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from fastapi import FastAPI\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider\n    from opentelemetry.trace import Span\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n# URLs whose server spans are never recorded. Same\n# posture as the request log: path only (#494).\n_URL_ATTRS: Final = (\"http.url\", \"http.target\", \"url.full\", \"url.query\")\n\n_provider: TracerProvider | None = None\n\n\ndef configure_tracing(service_name: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Install a TracerProvider exporting to App Insights, or no-op.\n\n    Idempotent per process (the global tracer provider can only be set once);\n    safe to call from both the API module scope and the Celery\n    worker-process-init signal.\n    \"\"\"\n    global _provider\n    if _provider is not None:\n        return\n    conn = get_settings().applicationinsights_connection_string\n    if not conn:\n        return\n\n    from azure.monitor.opentelemetry.exporter import AzureMonitorTraceExporter\n    from opentelemetry import trace\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider\n    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor\n\n    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({\"service.name\": service_name}))\n    provider.add_span_processor(\n        BatchSpanProcessor(AzureMonitorTraceExporter(connection_string=conn))\n    )\n    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)\n    _provider = provider\n    log.info(\"tracing_configured\", service_name=service_name)\n\n\ndef _scrub_query_hook(span: Span, scope: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"server_request_hook: overwrite URL-bearing attributes with the path only.\"\"\"\n    if span is None or not span.is_recording():\n        return\n    path = str(scope.get(\"path\", \"\"))\n    for attr in _URL_ATTRS:\n        span.set_attribute(attr, path if attr != \"url.query\" else \"\")\n\n\ndef instrument_fastapi(app: FastAPI) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit a server span per request (minus EXCLUDED_URLS). No-op when tracing is off.\n\n    MUST be called at module scope, before the app's first ASGI call — see the\n    module docstring's call-ordering constraint.\n    \"\"\"\n    if _provider is None:\n        return\n    from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor\n\n    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(\n        app,\n        tracer_provider=_provider,\n        excluded_urls=EXCLUDED_URLS,\n        server_request_hook=_scrub_query_hook,\n    )\n\n\ndef instrument_celery() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit a span per Celery task run/publish. 31	/**
32	 * Suite-detail panel for cron-driven run schedules (A7). A schedule runs the
33	 * suite unattended on a 5-field cron cadence in an IANA timezone — distinct from
34	 * Triggers (run-on-pipeline-success). Anyone with `view` sees the schedules;
35	 * `edit`+ (`canManage`) gets the create / pause-toggle / delete controls, matching
36	 * the backend gate. Cron/timezone are validated server-side (422 → inline error).
37	 */
38	export function SchedulesPanel({ suiteId, canManage }: { suiteId: string; canManage: boolean }) {
39	  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(() => listSchedules(suiteId));
40	
41	  return (
42	    <Card
43	      size="small"
44	      title={
45	        <Flex vertical gap={2}>
46	          <Typography.Text strong>Schedules</Typography.Text>
47	          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 400 }}>
48	            Run this suite automatically on a cron cadence.
49	          </Typography.Text>
50	        </Flex>
51	      }
52	    >
53	      <SchedulesBody state={state} suiteId={suiteId} canManage={canManage} onChanged={reload} />
54	    </Card>
55	  );
56	}
57	
58	function SchedulesBody({
59	  state,
60	  suiteId,
61	  canManage,
62	  onChanged,
63	}: {
64	  state: ReturnType<typeof useAsyncData<Schedule[]>>['state'];
65	  suiteId: string;
66	  canManage: boolean;
67	  onChanged: () => void;
68	}) {
69	  if (state.status === 'loading') {
70	    return <Spin description="Loading schedules…" />;
71	  }
72	  if (state.status === 'error') {
73	    return (
74	      <Alert type="error" showIcon title="Failed to load schedules" description={state.error} />
75	    );
76	  }
77	  const schedules = state.data;
78	
79	  return (
80	    <Flex vertical gap={16}>
81	      {canManage && <AddSchedule suiteId={suiteId} onAdded={onChanged} />}
82	      {schedules.length === 0 ? (
83	        <Empty
84	          image={Empty.PRESENTED_IMAGE_SIMPLE}
85	          description="No schedules — this suite runs only on manual / triggered runs."
86	        />
87	      ) : (
88	        <ScheduleTable schedules={schedules} canManage={canManage} onChanged={onChanged} />
89	      )}
90	    </Flex>
91	  );
92	}
93	
94	function ScheduleTable({
95	  schedules,
96	  canManage,
97	  onChanged,
98	}: {
99	  schedules: Schedule[];
100	  canManage: boolean;
101	  onChanged: () => void;
102	}) {
103	  const { message, modal } = App.useApp();
104	  const [busyId, setBusyId] = useState<string | null>(null);
105	
106	  // cron is not unique per row (the same cron can run in two timezones), so
107	  // identify a schedule by cron + timezone in labels/toasts/confirms.
108	  const label = (s: Schedule) => `${s.cron} (${s.timezone})`;
109	
110	  const onToggle = async (s: Schedule, enabled: boolean) => {
111	    setBusyId(s.id);
112	    try {
113	      await updateSchedule(s.id, { enabled });
114	      message.success(`${label(s)}: ${enabled ? 'resumed' : 'paused'}`);
115	      onChanged();
116	    } catch (err) {
117	      message.error(`Update failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
118	    } finally {
119	      setBusyId(null);
120	    }
121	  };
122	
123	  const onRemove = (s: Schedule) => {
124	    modal.confirm({
125	      title: `Delete schedule ${label(s)}?`,
126	      content: 'This suite will no longer run on this cadence.',
127	      okText: 'Delete',
128	      okType: 'danger',
129	      onOk: async () => {
130	        setBusyId(s.id);
131	        try {
132	          await deleteSchedule(s.id);
133	          message.success(`${label(s)}: removed`);
134	          onChanged();
135	        } catch (err) {
136	          message.error(`Remove failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
137	          throw err; // keep the confirm modal open on failure
138	        } finally {
139	          setBusyId(null);
140	        }
141	      },
142	    });
143	  };
144	
145	  const columns: ColumnsType<Schedule> = [
146	    {
147	      title: 'Cron',
148	      dataIndex: 'cron',
149	      render: (cron: string) => <Typography.Text code>{cron}</Typography.Text>,
150	    },
151	    { title: 'Timezone', dataIndex: 'timezone', width: 160 },
152	    {
153	      title: 'Next run',
154	      dataIndex: 'next_run_at',
155	      render: (t: string) => formatTimestamp(t),
156	    },
157	    {
158	      title: 'Last run',
159	      dataIndex: 'last_run_at',
160	      render: (t: string | null) => formatTimestamp(t),
161	    },
162	    {
163	      title: 'Status',
164	      dataIndex: 'enabled',
165	      width: 100,
166	      render: (enabled: boolean, s) =>
167	        canManage ? (
168	          <Switch
169	            size="small"
170	            checked={enabled}
171	            loading={busyId === s.id}
172	            onChange={(next) => onToggle(s, next)}
173	            aria-label={`${enabled ? 'Pause' : 'Resume'} ${label(s)}`}
174	          />
175	        ) : (
176	          <Tag color={enabled ? 'success' : 'default'}>{enabled ? 'enabled' : 'paused'}</Tag>
177	        ),
178	    },
179	    ...(canManage
180	      ? [
181	          {
182	            title: '',
183	            key: 'actions',
184	            width: 48,
185	            render: (_: unknown, s: Schedule) => (
186	              <Button
187	                size="small"
188	                type="text"
189	                danger
190	                icon={<DeleteOutlined />}
191	                loading={busyId === s.id}
192	                onClick={() => onRemove(s)}
193	                aria-label={`Remove ${label(s)}`}
194	              />
195	            ),
196	          },
197	        ]
198	      : []),
199	  ];
200	
201	  return (
202	    <Table<Schedule>
203	      rowKey="id"
204	      size="small"
205	      columns={columns}
206	      dataSource={schedules}
207	      pagination={false}
208	    />
209	  );
210	}
211	
212	function AddSchedule({ suiteId, onAdded }: { suiteId: string; onAdded: () => void }) {
213	  const { message } = App.useApp();
214	  const [cron, setCron] = useState('');
215	  const [timezone, setTimezone] = useState('UTC');
216	  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false);
217	  const zones = useMemo(() => timezoneOptions(), []);
218	
219	  const onAdd = async () => {
220	    const expr = cron.trim();
221	    if (!expr) return;
222	    setAdding(true);
223	    try {
224	      await createSchedule({ suite_id: suiteId, cron: expr, timezone });
225	      message.success(`${expr}: scheduled`);
226	      setCron('');
227	      onAdded();
228	    } catch (err) {
229	      message.error(`Add failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
230	    } finally {
231	      setAdding(false);
232	    }
233	  };
234	
235	  return (
236	    <Flex gap={8} align="center" wrap>
237	      <Input
238	        value={cron}
239	        onChange={(e) => setCron(e.target.value)}
240	        placeholder="Cron e.g. 0 9 * * 1-5 (min hour dom mon dow)"
241	        style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 220 }}
242	        onPressEnter={onAdd}
243	        aria-label="Cron expression"
244	      />
245	      <Select
246	        showSearch
247	        value={timezone}
248	        onChange={setTimezone}
249	        style={{ width: 220 }}
250	        options={zones.map((z) => ({ value: z, label: z }))}
251	        aria-label="Timezone"
252	      />
253	      <Button type="primary" loading={adding} disabled={!cron.trim()} onClick={onAdd}>
254	        Add
255	      </Button>
256	    </Flex>
257	  );
258	}

35	 * providers are never a datasource; this is the one place a pipeline id meets a
36	 * suite). Anyone with `view` sees the bindings; `edit`+ (`canManage`) gets the
37	 * add / enable-toggle / remove controls, matching the backend gate.
38	 */
39	export function TriggersPanel({ suiteId, canManage }: { suiteId: string; canManage: boolean }) {
40	  const { state, reload } = useAsyncData(() => listTriggerBindings(suiteId));
41	
42	  return (
43	    <Card
44	      size="small"
45	      title={
46	        <Flex vertical gap={2}>
47	          <Typography.Text strong>Triggers</Typography.Text>
48	          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 400 }}>
49	            Run this suite when an orchestrator pipeline / DAG completes successfully.
50	          </Typography.Text>
51	        </Flex>
52	      }
53	    >
54	      <TriggersBody state={state} suiteId={suiteId} canManage={canManage} onChanged={reload} />
55	    </Card>
56	  );
57	}

59	function TriggersBody({
60	  state,
61	  suiteId,
62	  canManage,
63	  onChanged,
64	}: {
65	  state: ReturnType<typeof useAsyncData<TriggerBinding[]>>['state'];
66	  suiteId: string;
67	  canManage: boolean;
68	  onChanged: () => void;
69	}) {

71	    return <Spin description="Loading triggers…" />;
72	  }
73	  if (state.status === 'error') {
74	    return (

76	    );

79	
80	  return (
81	    <Flex vertical gap={16}>
82	      {canManage && <AddTrigger suiteId={suiteId} onAdded={onChanged} />}
83	      {bindings.length === 0 ? (

86	          description="No triggers — this suite runs only on manual / scheduled runs."

96	              onChanged={onChanged}

98	          )}
99	        />
100	      )}
101	    </Flex>
102	  );
103	}

105	function TriggerRow({

187	function AddTrigger({ suiteId, onAdded }: { suiteId: string; onAdded: () => void }) {
188	  const { message } = App.useApp();

199	      await createTriggerBinding({ provider, env, pipeline_or_dag_id: id, suite_id: suiteId });
200	      message.success(`${id}: trigger added`);

203	      setPipelineId('');
204	      onAdded();
205	    } catch (err) {

207	    } finally {

209	    }
210	  };

1	# Browser E2E (Playwright)
2	
3	Drives the **real app in a browser** under dev-bypass auth against the seeded
4	demo dataset — the other half of the full-stack smoke (#128). The httpx API
5	smoke (`backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py`) proves `HTTP → service → DB`; this proves
6	the React UI a user actually clicks: `browser → Vite proxy → api → DB`.
7	
8	> Live `test()`/runs against real Snowflake/S3/etc. stay out of scope (no creds
9	> locally — the documented deferred smoke). The connectivity tests here
10	> **fail-soft**; the specs assert the health/error path renders, not that a real
11	> datasource is reachable.
12	
13	## Run it locally
14	
15	1. Bring up the stack and seed the demo data:
16	
17	   ```bash
18	   docker compose up -d            # postgres + redis + api + worker + frontend
19	   conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
20	   ```
21	
22	2. Install browsers once, then run:
23	
24	   ```bash
25	   cd frontend
26	   pnpm install
27	   pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
28	   pnpm e2e            # headless
29	   pnpm e2e:ui         # Playwright UI mode (watch/debug)
30	   ```
31	
32	The config (`playwright.config.ts`) targets `E2E_BASE_URL` (default
33	`http://localhost:3000`) and **reuses** the already-running compose/`pnpm dev`
34	server on :3000. Point it elsewhere with `E2E_BASE_URL=… pnpm e2e`.
35	
36	## In CI
37	
38	The `frontend-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` spins up Postgres + Redis,
39	pip-installs the backend, runs migrations, seeds the demo data, launches
40	`uvicorn` on :8000, then lets Playwright start its own Vite dev server on :3000
41	(`VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET=http://localhost:8000`) and run the specs. No Azure /
42	real datasource credentials are involved — dev-bypass only.
43	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/e2e/schedules.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';\n\n// SchedulesPanel (A7) on the seeded suite's detail page: full authoring\n// round-trip (add → pause → delete) plus the server-side cron validation\n// path (422 → error toast, no row). The dispatcher itself (60s beat) is\n// backend-tested; this proves the UI a user actually drives.\ntest.describe('Suite schedules panel', () => {\n  // Distinctive cron so leftovers from an aborted local run can't collide\n  // with the seeded data; the test deletes it on the way out.\n  const CRON = '7 3 * * 2';\n\n  const card = (page: import('@playwright/test').Page) =>\n    page.locator('.ant-card').filter({ hasText: 'cron cadence' });\n\n  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/suites');\n    await page.getByText('Orders quality').click();\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\\/suites\\/[0-9a-f-]+$/);\n    await expect(card(page).getByText('Schedules', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  test('rejects an invalid cron with an error toast and no row', async ({ page }) => {\n    const panel = card(page);\n    await panel.getByLabel('Cron expression').fill('not a cron');\n    await panel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' }).click();\n\n    // Server-side validation (422) surfaces as the panel's error toast.\n    await expect(page.getByText(/Add failed/)).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(panel.locator('tr.ant-table-row').filter({ hasText: 'not a cron' })).toHaveCount(\n      0,\n    );\n  });\n\n  test('add a schedule, pause it, then delete it', async ({ page }) => {\n    const panel = card(page);\n\n    // Add (timezone stays the UTC default).\n    await panel.getByLabel('Cron expression').fill(CRON);\n    await panel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' }).click();\n    const row = panel.locator('tr.ant-table-row').filter({ hasText: CRON });\n    await expect(row).toHaveCount(1);\n    // The dispatcher precomputed the next run; the cell is populated.\n    await expect(row.getByText(/\\d{4}|\\d{2}:\\d{2}/).first()).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Pause via the status switch — toast carries the cron (timezone) label.\n    await row.getByRole('switch').click();\n    await expect(page.getByText(`${CRON} (UTC): paused`)).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Delete → confirm modal → the row disappears.\n    await row.getByRole('button', { name: `Remove ${CRON} (UTC)` }).click();\n    const confirm = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /^Delete schedule/ });\n    await confirm.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' }).click();\n    await expect(panel.locator('tr.ant-table-row').filter({ hasText: CRON })).toHaveCount(0);\n  });\n});\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/e2e/trigger-bindings.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';\n\n// TriggersPanel on the seeded suite's detail page: bind an orchestrator\n// pipeline (run-on-success, CLAUDE.md §4 — the one place a pipeline id meets a\n// suite), toggle it, and remove it. The binding is provider-agnostic\n// (`trigger_bindings`); the seeded ADF/Airflow connections make the providers\n// real, and a unique pipeline id keeps the composite key (provider, id, env)\n// collision-free across runs.\ntest.describe('Suite triggers panel', () => {\n  const card = (page: import('@playwright/test').Page) =>\n    page.locator('.ant-card').filter({ hasText: 'orchestrator pipeline' });\n\n  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto('/suites');\n    await page.getByText('Orders quality').click();\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\\/suites\\/[0-9a-f-]+$/);\n    await expect(card(page).getByText('Triggers', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n  });\n\n  test('bind a pipeline, disable it, then remove it', async ({ page }) => {\n    const panel = card(page);\n    const pipelineId = `e2e_pl_${Date.now()}`;\n\n    // Provider + Env are antd Selects: focus the combobox, wait for the\n    // dropdown, keyboard-select the first option (stable against rc-virtual-\n    // list measurement, same pattern as suites.spec.ts). DOM order within the\n    // panel: [0]=Provider ('adf' first), [1]=Env ('dev' first).\n    const combos = panel.getByRole('combobox');\n    await combos.first().click();\n    await expect(page.locator('.ant-select-dropdown').last()).toBeVisible();\n    await combos.first().press('ArrowDown');\n    await combos.first().press('Enter');\n\n    await panel.getByPlaceholder('Pipeline / DAG id').fill(pipelineId);\n\n    await combos.nth(1).click();\n    await expect(page.locator('.ant-select-dropdown').last()).toBeVisible();\n    await combos.nth(1).press('ArrowDown');\n    await combos.nth(1).press('Enter');\n\n    await panel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText(`${pipelineId}: trigger added`)).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Listed with its provider label and enabled by default.\n    const row = panel.locator('[role=\"listitem\"]').filter({ hasText: pipelineId });\n    await expect(row).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(row.getByText('Azure Data Factory')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(row.getByRole('switch')).toBeChecked();\n\n    // Disable (run-on-success stops firing without losing the binding).\n    await row.getByRole('switch').click();\n    await expect(page.getByText(`${pipelineId}: disabled`)).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Remove — immediate (no confirm) — and the row disappears.\n    await row.getByRole('button', { name: `Remove ${pipelineId}` }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText(`${pipelineId}: removed`)).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(panel.locator('[role=\"listitem\"]').filter({ hasText: pipelineId })).toHaveCount(\n      0,\n    );\n  });\n});\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/e2e/notifications.spec.ts",
  "content": "import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';\n\n// NotificationsPanel on the seeded suite's detail page: per-suite alerting\n// config (W6 — fronts notification_service). Sets a deterministic state\n// (enabled + warn threshold), saves, and proves it survives a reload. The\n// Teams webhook stays untouched — it's write-only (the API never returns it)\n// and writing one would push a secret into the store; the spec only asserts\n// the write-only affordance renders.\ntest.describe('Suite notifications panel', () => {\n  const card = (page: import('@playwright/test').Page) =>\n    page.locator('.ant-card').filter({ hasText: 'run outcomes to Microsoft Teams' });\n\n  const openSuite = async (page: import('@playwright/test').Page) => {\n    await page.goto('/suites');\n    await page.getByText('Orders quality').click();\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\\/suites\\/[0-9a-f-]+$/);\n    await expect(card(page).getByText('Notifications', { exact: true })).toBeVisible();\n  };\n\n  test('configure threshold routing and persist it across a reload', async ({ page }) => {\n    await openSuite(page);\n    const panel = card(page);\n\n    // Deterministic target state: enabled + \"On warn and worse\".\n    const enable = panel.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Enable notifications' });\n    if (!(await enable.isChecked())) {\n      await enable.click();\n    }\n    const threshold = panel.getByRole('combobox');\n    await threshold.click();\n    await expect(page.locator('.ant-select-dropdown').last()).toBeVisible();\n    await page.getByRole('option', { name: 'On warn and worse' }).click();\n\n    await panel.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();\n    await expect(page.getByText('Notifications saved')).toBeVisible();\n\n    // Reload → the form re-seeds from the API with the saved values.\n    await page.reload();\n    await expect(card(page).getByText('On warn and worse')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(card(page).getByRole('switch', { name: 'Enable notifications' })).toBeChecked();\n  });\n\n  test('webhook is a write-only secret affordance', async ({ page }) => {\n    await openSuite(page);\n    const panel = card(page);\n\n    // The field never echoes a stored URL — just a set/not-set tag + password\n    // input. (Writing one is out of scope: it lands a secret in the store.)\n    await expect(panel.getByText('Teams webhook')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(panel.getByLabel('Teams webhook URL')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(panel.getByText(/^(set|not set)$/)).toBeVisible();\n  });\n});\n"
}

593-
594-    * numeric summary keys (`unexpected_count` / `unexpected_percent`) always pass;
595-    * `partial_unexpected_list` (the tested column's scalar failing values) passes when
596-      the tested column is **not known sensitive** — so a non-PII breach (a bad
597-      ``LINE_TOTAL``) is *visible* while a PII tested column (``email``) stays masked;
598-      with **no** ``tested_column`` the list is masked (no column context → safe default);
599-    * row-dicts (`unexpected_index_list`, or a dict-shaped `partial_unexpected_list`)

const PROVIDER_LABELS: Record<string, string> = { adf: 'Azure Data Factory', airflow: 'Airflow' };

/** One provider's webhook URL. ADF embeds a secret, so it's masked behind a reveal
 *  toggle; copy always copies the real URL. */
function WebhookRow({ webhook }: { webhook: AdminWebhook }) {
  const [revealed, setRevealed] = useState(false);
  const secretBearing = webhook.provider === 'adf';
  // Mask only the token value, keeping the rest of the URL legible.
  const display =
    secretBearing && !revealed
      ? webhook.inbound_url.replace(/token=[^&]*/i, 'token=••••••••')
      : webhook.inbound_url;
  return (
    <Card
      size="small"
      type="inner"
      title={
        <Flex align="center" gap={8}>
          <Tag color={secretBearing ? 'geekblue' : 'cyan'}>
            {PROVIDER_LABELS[webhook.provider] ?? webhook.provider}
          </Tag>
          {secretBearing && !webhook.token_configured && (
            <Tag color="error">webhook secret not set</Tag>
          )}
        </Flex>
      }
    >
      <Flex vertical gap={8}>
        <Flex align="center" gap={8}>
          <Input readOnly value={display} style={{ fontFamily: 'monospace' }} />
          {secretBearing && (
            <Button
              icon={revealed ? <EyeInvisibleOutlined /> : <EyeOutlined />}
              onClick={() => setRevealed((r) => !r)}
              title={revealed ? 'Hide token' : 'Reveal token'}
            />
          )}
          <Typography.Text copyable={{ text: webhook.inbound_url }} />
        </Flex>
        <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
          {webhook.auth}
        </Typography.Text>
        {secretBearing ? (
          <Typography.Text type="secondary" style={{ fontSize: 12 }}>
            Paste into Azure Monitor → Action Group → Webhook. Live delivery also needs the
            Common-Alert-Schema payload mapping (#492).

1	# Datasources & checks
2	
3	## Supported datasources
4	
5	| Datasource | Connection | Check authoring | Execution |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT) | account + user + key/PAT | ✅ | ✅ |
8	| ADLS Gen2 (flat files) | account URL + container, SAS | ✅ | ✅ |
9	| AWS S3 (flat files) | bucket + region, access key | ✅ | ✅ |
10	| Unity Catalog (Databricks) | workspace URL + warehouse + PAT | ✅ | ✅ |
11	
12	## Add a connection
13	
14	In the UI, **Connections → Add connection**, pick the datasource, fill the type-specific
15	fields, and **Test** it (a live reachability probe). Credentials are stored in the secret
16	store (Azure Key Vault in production), never in the database.
17	
18	## Author a check
19	
20	1. Create (or open) a **suite** and point it at a **target** — a table (Snowflake/UC), a
21	   file/path or batch pattern (ADLS/S3).
22	2. **Add a check.** Two paths:
23	   - **Form** — pick a Great Expectations expectation (e.g.
24	     `expect_column_values_to_not_be_null`) + column + optional warn/fail/critical
25	     thresholds.
26	   - **Custom SQL** — a read-only SQL rule (rows returned = failures), for SQL datasources.
27	   - **Monitors** — *freshness* (is the table stale?) and *volume* (row-count in range?)
28	     on SQL datasources.
29	3. **Dry-run** to preview pass/fail before saving; use the **column profiler** (nulls,
30	   distinct count, min/max, top values) to decide thresholds.
31	
32	## Run it
33	
34	Run a suite **now**, on a **cron schedule**, or **triggered** by a pipeline (see
35	**[Orchestration](orchestration.md)**). Results land on the **Results** page and the
36	**Dashboard** (health score + trends); failures alert per the suite's notification config.
37	
38	Severity comes from thresholds banding the observed unexpected-percentage
39	(warn < fail < critical); see ADR 0005 / 0016 for the model.
40	
```

==> backend/app/alerting/routing.py <==
"""Severity-aware routing — *whether* and *how loudly* to alert on a run.

The single policy point between a built ``RunReport`` and the channel: it maps
the run's worst severity to a ``Route`` (send-or-not + urgency + whether to
escalate to the whole channel). The publisher delegates the send decision here,
and the card renders the urgency, so "warn is quiet, fail is standard, critical
pings the channel" lives in one place rather than smeared across the publisher
and the renderer.

Per-suite policy (alert on fail / warn / always) extends this in a later PR by
folding the suite's preference into ``route_for`` — the publisher and card don't
change.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport

# Urgency levels, quietest first. The card maps these to colour + escalation.
QUIET = "quiet"
STANDARD = "standard"
CRITICAL = "critical"

# Per-suite delivery policies (mirror db.models.ALERT_ON_POLICIES). The default
# preserves the pre-config behaviour: alert on warn+ but not on clean runs.
FAIL_ONLY = "fail"
WARN_PLUS = "warn"
ALWAYS = "always"
DEFAULT_POLICY = WARN_PLUS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Route:
    """The routing decision for one run.

    ``should_send`` gates delivery; ``urgency`` drives the card's prominence;
    ``mention_channel`` escalates a critical breach to the whole channel.
    """

==> backend/app/alerting/dedup.py <==
"""Alert dedup — fire on the *first* failure, not every subsequent run.

A failing check on a scheduled suite would otherwise alert on every run while it
stays broken. This compares a run's failing checks to the suite's **previous
terminal run** and suppresses the alert when nothing got worse: a new alert
fires only when a check starts failing (or escalates severity) relative to last
time. Recovery (a clean run) resets the baseline, so the next failure re-fires.

Derived from run history — **no new state / migration**. The unit is per-check
(by ``check_id``, not name, so a renamed check still dedups), which is why this
reads ``results`` directly rather than the name-only ``RunReport``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import select, tuple_
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.db.models import Result, Run

# Failing severity tiers → rank (higher = worse). `pass`/`skip`/`error` aren't
# alert-worthy and never appear here.
_RANK = {"warn": 1, "fail": 2, "critical": 3}
# An operational run failure (the adapter raised — no per-check result rows) is a
# single suite-level failure signature, keyed by this sentinel, ranked at fail.
_OPERATIONAL_KEY = "__run__"
_OPERATIONAL_RANK = 2


def _failing_ranks(session: Session, run: Run) -> dict[str, int]:
    """The failing checks of ``run`` as ``{check_id: rank}`` (escalation-aware).

    An executed run contributes its breaching per-check results; a run that
    *failed to execute* (no results) contributes one suite-level signature so two
    consecutive operational failures still dedup.
    """
    rows = session.execute(
        select(Result.check_id, Result.status).where(Result.run_id == run.id)
    ).all()
    ranks = {str(check_id): _RANK[status] for check_id, status in rows if status in _RANK}

window. This answers the one question the dispatch layer needs: *are all of this
run's failing checks currently snoozed?* If so, the alert is suppressed; if even
```

1	# Observability & troubleshooting
2	
3	## Logs & telemetry
4	
5	- **Structured JSON logs** (structlog) everywhere, with a `request_id` correlated across
6	  FastAPI → Celery → Great Expectations. **PII is redacted at the logger level**, so
7	  failed-check sample rows can't leak into logs.
8	- **Azure Application Insights** captures logs + exceptions in deployed environments
9	  (gated on the connection string; off locally).
10	
11	## Where to look
12	
13	- **Dashboard** — workspace health score, pass-rate, run counts, and trends.
14	- **Results** — every run, drill into per-check pass/fail with observed-vs-expected and
15	  (PII-redacted) sample failing rows; a **Pipelines** tab correlates orchestration runs.
16	- **Run progress** — live check-by-check status for an in-flight run.
17	
18	## Common failures
19	
20	| Symptom | Likely cause / fix |
21	|---|---|
22	| Run stuck `queued` | Broker (Redis) unreachable at dispatch. A beat **reaper** fails runs left non-terminal past a threshold; re-run once the worker/broker is healthy. |
23	| Connection **Test** fails | Bad/expired credential or network egress — re-authenticate the connection; check the secret store. |
24	| Pipeline didn't trigger a suite | Only **successful** runs trigger; confirm an **enabled trigger binding** matches `(provider, pipeline/DAG, env)`. |
25	| Checks all `skip` on a flat-file suite | The batch hasn't landed yet (no matching file) — expected; the run succeeds with skips. |
26	| Orchestration events not arriving | Webhook secret/HMAC mismatch — the 10-min poll is the fallback; verify the connection's secret. |
27	
28	## Operating notes
29	
30	After a shared-Postgres delete/recreate, **restart dependent Container Apps** (the DB host
31	is a start-time secret snapshot). Full deploy + ops runbook:
32	[`deploy/README.md`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md).
33

1	# Orchestration integration (ADF & Airflow)
2	
3	DataQ **observes** your pipelines and can **run check suites when they finish** — it does
4	not run the pipelines. Both Azure Data Factory and Apache Airflow sit behind one
5	`OrchestrationProvider` interface, so the behaviour is identical.
6	
7	## What DataQ does with a pipeline
8	
9	1. **Monitor** — every pipeline/DAG run is recorded in `pipeline_runs`.
10	2. **Detect failures** near-real-time via a webhook, with a 10-minute polling fallback.
11	3. **Trigger on success** — if a successful run matches an enabled **trigger binding**
12	   (`provider` + `pipeline/DAG id` + `env` → `suite_id`), DataQ queues that suite.
13	   *Failures alert but never trigger a run.*
14	
15	## ADF
16	
17	Azure Monitor raises an alert on pipeline events → an **Action Group webhook** POSTs to
18	`/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf` (shared-secret authenticated). Succeeded runs are also
19	picked up by the 10-min poll against the ADF REST API. To get the exact webhook URL to
20	paste into the Action Group (host + `?token=` secret, assembled from the live deployment
21	and Key Vault rather than by hand), see **One-time provisioning → step 5** in the
22	[deployment guide](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/deploy/README.md).
23	
24	## Airflow
25	
26	Add the provided callback snippet
27	([`integrations/airflow/`](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/tree/main/integrations/airflow))
28	to your DAGs — its `on_success_callback` / `on_failure_callback` HMAC-signs and POSTs to
29	`/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow`. Polling the Airflow REST API is the fallback.
30	
31	## Wiring a trigger
32	
33	In the UI, open a suite's **Triggers** and bind it to a `(provider, pipeline/DAG, env)`.
34	When that pipeline next succeeds, the suite runs automatically and you'll see the run
35	correlated to the pipeline run on the **Results → Pipelines** view.
36

1	# DataQ
2	
3	> Data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations — Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog (Databricks), with ADF + Airflow orchestration integrations.
4	
5	**📖 Documentation site: <https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/>** (MkDocs Material — quickstart, concepts, architecture, guides).
6	
7	**Status:** pre-v1 — Week 7 (deployment, hardening & docs). Weeks 1–6 complete; v1 is **deployed to Azure Container Apps** — API + worker + a runtime-configured **frontend Container App** (the sole public surface; the api runs on internal ingress behind it), with Key Vault, App Insights, and orchestration polling live. Auth is a **generic OIDC client** (validated against Azure AD; ADR [0028](docs/adr/0028-cloud-neutral-image-runtime-config-generic-oidc.md)). Live task-level progress at [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md).
8	
9	## Stack
10	
11	| Layer | Tech |
12	|---|---|
13	| Backend | FastAPI · Celery · Great Expectations · SQLAlchemy + Alembic · PostgreSQL · Redis |
14	| Frontend | React · Vite · Ant Design · generic OIDC (`oidc-client-ts`) |
15	| Auth / secrets | OIDC — Azure AD validated (`AUTH_*` contract, provider-neutral) · Azure Key Vault |
16	| Hosting | Azure Container Apps (API · worker · frontend) + Application Insights (deployed) |
17	| AI integration | FastMCP — 8 curated MCP tools at `/mcp` for Claude Desktop / Copilot / Cursor |
18	
19	## Quick start
20	
21	### Run DataQ — prebuilt images (recommended)
22	
23	Evaluate or self-host in ~5 minutes: **no source checkout, no Azure tenant.** Just Docker.
24	
25	```bash
26	curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/main/docker-compose.ghcr.yml
27	docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up
28	```
29	
30	Open **<http://localhost:3000>** — the stack comes up migrated and seeded with demo data, on **dev-bypass auth** (every request is a fixed demo user; no sign-in). API + Swagger at `http://localhost:8000/docs`. Images are pulled from GHCR and are **multi-arch** (amd64 + arm64), so Apple-Silicon runs native. Ports bind to `127.0.0.1` only. To pin a release instead of the moving tags: `DATAQ_BACKEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z DATAQ_FRONTEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up`.
31	
32	> Self-hosting with **your own** Azure AD? The published frontend is **one generic image** — the compose eval runs it with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (auth off). For real SSO, **no rebuild**: run that same image with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` + `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (auth config is injected at runtime, ADR 0028), and run the backend with `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` off. See [Getting started](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/getting-started/).
33	
34	### Develop DataQ — from source
35	
36	```bash
37	git clone https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ.git
38	cd DataQ
39	./scripts/setup.sh       # conda env + pre-commit + docker-compose + migrations
40	conda activate dataq
41	docker-compose up
42	```
43	
44	Backend at `http://localhost:8000` (Swagger at `/docs`), frontend at `http://localhost:3000`.
45	
46	## MCP (AI assistant access)
47	
48	DataQ exposes 8 curated MCP tools at `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) — `list_suites`, `get_suite_results`, `get_health_score`, `get_adf_pipeline_status`, `trigger_suite_run`, `get_run_status`, `create_check`, `profile_column`. The endpoint is **Azure AD–protected**: present the same bearer token the web UI uses (validated against the same tenant / audience / scope). Without Azure auth configured the endpoint is only mounted in local dev-bypass mode — never unauthenticated in a deployed environment (ADR [0008](docs/adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).
49	
50	Point any MCP client at `https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp` with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
51	
52	**Claude Desktop / Claude.ai** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) — and **GitHub Copilot** (`mcp.json`):
53	
54	```jsonc
55	{
56	  "mcpServers": {
57	    "dataq": {
58	      "url": "https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp",
59	      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <AZURE_AD_ACCESS_TOKEN>" }
60	    }
61	  }
62	}
63	```
64	
65	**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) uses the same `mcpServers` shape. Once configured, all 8 tools are available to natural-language queries (e.g. *"what failed in the orders suite today?"*, *"run the orders suite on DEV"*).
66

74	| **Project guide for AI assistants** | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) |
75	| **Architecture diagram + invariants** | [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) |
76	| **Architecture Decision Records** | [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) |
77	| **Live task tracker** | [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) |
78	| **Product roadmap (8 weeks, 100 tasks)** | [context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md](context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md) |
79	| **Security policy + responsible disclosure** | [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md) |
80

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/notifications.md",
  "content": "# Notifications & alerting\n\nDataQ alerts on run outcomes over **Microsoft Teams**, **Slack**, and **email** — all\nbehind one `ResultPublisher` seam, so every channel gets the same severity-aware\nbehaviour. Alerts fire from the worker as soon as a run reaches a terminal state.\n\n## Channels\n\n| Channel | Configured by | How |\n|---|---|---|\n| Microsoft Teams | Workspace default **or per-suite override** | Incoming-webhook URL; the per-suite URL is set on the suite's **Notifications** panel (write-only — stored in the secret store, never echoed back) |\n| Slack | Workspace | Incoming-webhook URL (secret store) |\n| Email (SMTP) | Workspace | SMTP host/port + from/to + password secret |\n\nWorkspace-level channels are enabled by environment configuration\n(`TEAMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME`, `SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME`, `EMAIL_*` — see the\n[env-var reference](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/.env.app.example)).\nA channel with no configuration is simply skipped; configuring none disables alerting.\nWebhook URLs are validated against an allow-list of hosts (`webhook.office.com`,\n`hooks.slack.com`, …) so a typo can't exfiltrate alerts to an arbitrary endpoint.\n\n## Per-suite configuration\n\nOpen a suite → **Notifications** panel:\n\n- **Send alerts for this suite** — on/off.\n- **Alert threshold** — `On fail / critical` · `On warn and worse` (default) · `Always\n  (every run)`.\n- **Teams webhook** — optional per-suite override of the workspace webhook. Write-only:\n  the tag shows *set / not set*, the URL is never displayed again.\n\n## Severity-aware routing\n\nThe run's **worst severity** decides how loudly the alert lands: `warn` renders quiet,\n`fail` standard, and `critical` escalates (channel mention on Teams). A run that\n**failed to execute** (the datasource was unreachable, the adapter raised) always\nalerts regardless of the suite's threshold — an operational failure is never filtered\nas \"no warn-level breach\".\n\n## Dedup — first failure, not every run\n\nA broken check on a 15-minute schedule would otherwise page you 96 times a day. DataQ\ncompares each run's failing checks to the suite's **previous terminal run** and alerts\nonly when something got **worse**: a check newly failing, or escalating severity\n(warn → fail → critical). A clean run resets the baseline, so the *next* regression\nre-fires. No configuration needed.\n\n## Snooze / suppression\n\nSnooze a specific check's alerts for N hours from the suite's check list (e.g. during a\nknown upstream incident). A run alerts only if at least one **un-snoozed** check is\nfailing; when every failing check is snoozed, the alert is suppressed. Snoozes expire\nautomatically.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Check |\n|---|---|\n| No alert on a failing run | Suite panel: enabled? threshold covers the severity? Dedup: did the *same* checks already fail in the previous run? All failing checks snoozed? |\n| Teams/Slack alert rejected | Webhook host must be on the allowed-hosts list; the URL secret must exist in the secret store. |\n| Alert on every run wanted | Set the suite's threshold to **Always (every run)** — dedup still applies to failures, but clean runs report too. |\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/scheduling.md",
  "content": "# Scheduling suite runs\n\nThree ways to run a suite: **manually** (Run now), on a **cron schedule** (this page),\nor **triggered by a pipeline** (see [Orchestration](orchestration.md)). Prefer a\ntrigger binding when an orchestrator loads the data — the checks run right after the\nload, not at a guessed time; schedule when there's no orchestrator (e.g. flat-file\ndrops on ADLS/S3).\n\n## Add a schedule\n\nOpen a suite → **Schedules** panel → enter a cron expression + timezone → **Add**.\nA suite can hold several schedules (e.g. hourly on weekdays + a daily deep pass).\n\n- **Cron** is standard 5-field (`minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`):\n  - `0 9 * * 1-5` — 09:00 on weekdays\n  - `*/30 * * * *` — every 30 minutes\n  - `0 6 1 * *` — 06:00 on the 1st of each month\n  Invalid expressions are rejected on save.\n- **Timezone** is a full IANA zone (`Europe/London`, `Asia/Kolkata`, …), so `0 9 * * *`\n  means 9 AM *local to that zone* — **DST-aware** (the schedule shifts with the zone's\n  clock changes, not with UTC).\n\n## Semantics worth knowing\n\n- **Minute granularity.** A dispatcher ticks every 60 s and fires schedules whose\n  precomputed next-run time has passed — sub-minute cadences aren't supported.\n- **No backfill.** If the platform was down across N ticks, those runs are **not**\n  replayed on startup; the schedule simply resumes at its next occurrence. (Missed\n  *orchestration events* are different — those have gap recovery.)\n- **Pause / resume** with the status switch — the schedule and its cadence are kept,\n  delivery stops.\n- **Stuck-run safety net.** A run orphaned in `queued`/`running` (dead worker, broker\n  hiccup) is failed by a reaper after a threshold, so a schedule can't wedge the suite.\n\n## Where results land\n\nScheduled runs appear on **Results** and the **Dashboard** like any other run, with\n`triggered_by` marking the schedule. Alerting applies per the suite's\n[notification config](notifications.md).\n"
}

  "content": "# Feature matrix\n\nOne-page reference: what runs where. For the concepts behind the columns, see\n[Concepts](concepts.md) and [Datasources & checks](datasources-checks.md).\n\n## Check kinds × datasources\n\n| Check kind | Snowflake | Unity Catalog | ADLS Gen2 (files) | S3 (files) |\n|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|\n| GX expectations (column / table shape) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Custom SQL (rows returned = failures) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |\n| Freshness monitor (hours since latest timestamp) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |\n| Volume monitor (row count in range) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |\n| Column profiler (nulls, distinct, min/max, top values) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Dry-run preview | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n\nCustom SQL and the freshness/volume monitors run a SQL query, so they're **SQL-datasource\nonly** (flat-file support is a tracked enhancement,\n[#520](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/520)). Flat-file suites target a\nfile or a batch pattern (e.g. `orders_*.csv`) in CSV or Parquet.\n\n## Ways a suite runs\n\n| Mode | Where | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Run now | Suite detail → Run panel | Live per-check progress + cancel |\n| Cron schedule | Suite detail → Schedules | 5-field cron, IANA timezone, DST-aware, [no backfill](scheduling.md) |\n| Pipeline trigger | Suite detail → Triggers | Runs on a pipeline/DAG **success** — ADF + Airflow, see [Orchestration](orchestration.md) |\n| API / MCP | `POST /suites/{id}/run` · `trigger_suite_run` MCP tool | Same authz as the UI |\n\n## Severity & results\n\n| Capability | Notes |\n|---|---|\n| Severity tiers | warn / fail / critical, banded from the observed unexpected-% (ADR 0005/0016) |\n| Operational statuses | `error` (evaluation threw) and `skip` (precondition unmet) are distinct from failures |\n| Health score | Severity-weighted, on the Dashboard |\n| Failing-row samples | Redacted column-aware before display (suite column policy + classifier) |\n| Run history retention | Samples purged after the retention window; metric trends kept |\n\n## Alerting\n\n| Capability | Notes |\n|---|---|\n| Channels | Teams (workspace + per-suite webhook), Slack, email — [details](notifications.md) |\n| Threshold | Per suite: fail-only / warn+ (default) / always |\n| Routing | Severity-aware urgency; critical escalates |\n| Dedup | First failure / escalation only; clean run resets |\n| Snooze | Per check, N hours |\n\n## Orchestration providers (not datasources)\n\n| Provider | Failure detection | Trigger on success |\n|---|---|---|\n| Azure Data Factory | Azure Monitor alert → webhook (+10-min poll) | ✅ trigger bindings |\n| Apache Airflow | DAG callback → HMAC webhook (+10-min poll) | ✅ trigger bindings |\n\n## Interfaces\n\n| Surface | What |\n|---|---|\n| Web UI | Dashboard · Connections · Suites · Results · Profile · Admin · Settings |\n| REST API | Versioned `/api/v1` (Swagger in non-prod) |\n| MCP | 8 curated tools at `/mcp` for AI assistants (ADR 0008) |\n"
}

{
