"""downgrade legacy admin shares to edit (ADR 0027 / #482)

Revision ID: e5f6a7b8c9d0
Revises: d4e5f6a7b8c9
Create Date: 2026-06-30 02:00:00.000000+00:00

ADR 0027 removes grantable suite-``admin``: a normal user can only hold a
``view``/``edit`` share, and ``admin`` is now the *workspace-admin* (implicit on
every suite, never a ``shares`` row). The step-1 code stopped issuing new
``admin`` shares (the ``SharePermission`` Literal is ``view|edit`` and
``share_service`` rejects anything else) but deliberately kept reading any
pre-existing ``shares.permission = 'admin'`` rows as ``admin`` so nobody lost
access between the two deploys (backward-compatible).

This migration retires those legacy rows by downgrading them to ``edit`` — the
closest non-removed capability (they keep check-authoring/run access, lose
manage-shares/delete, which is now workspace-admin-only). After this runs there
should be no ``admin`` share rows; the new grant path already can't create more.

**Not a schema change.** The ``permission_valid`` CHECK still lists ``admin``
(``models.PERMISSIONS`` is unchanged) so the value stays legal at the DB layer —
this keeps a rollback to step-1 code safe and is harmless once the rows are gone.

**Tested up + down locally.** Down is a deliberate no-op: the original set of
``admin`` grantees is not recoverable (we can't tell which ``edit`` rows were
once ``admin``), and the affected users retain a valid ``edit`` share either way,
so there is no access regression to reverse. A rollback that genuinely needs the
old admins back must re-grant them out of band (and, pre-ADR-0027, via code that
still allowed it).
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence

from alembic import op

# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
revision: str = "e5f6a7b8c9d0"
down_revision: str | None = "d4e5f6a7b8c9"
branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None
depends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None


def upgrade() -> None:
    op.execute("UPDATE shares SET permission = 'edit' WHERE permission = 'admin'")
```

  "content": "\"\"\"results.check_id -> ON DELETE CASCADE (#540)\n\nRevision ID: a9b0c1d2e3f4\nRevises: e5f6a7b8c9d0\nCreate Date: 2026-07-02 04:00:00.000000+00:00\n\n``results.check_id`` was the only FK in the schema without an ``ondelete``, so\ndeleting a suite whose checks have result rows hit\n``fk_results_check_id_checks`` (the suites→checks cascade fires while\nruns→results rows still reference the checks) and the API 500'd — any suite\nthat had ever run could not be deleted. Found by the Week-7 live smoke.\n\nCASCADE matches the schema's posture everywhere else (ADR 0020: cascade-delete\naccepted; ``results.run_id`` already cascades), and changes nothing about\nresult retention outside the delete path: results already die with their run.\n\n**Backward-compatible**: constraint drop + recreate only, no column change;\nold code keeps working during a rolling deploy. **Tested up + down locally.**\nDown restores the original NO ACTION constraint (rows deleted by a cascade in\nthe interim are gone, as accepted by ADR 0020).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\n\nfrom alembic import op\n\n# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.\nrevision: str = \"a9b0c1d2e3f4\"\ndown_revision: str | None = \"e5f6a7b8c9d0\"\nbranch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None\ndepends_on: str | Sequence[str] | None = None\n\n_FK = \"fk_results_check_id_checks\"\n\n\ndef upgrade() -> None:\n    op.drop_constraint(_FK, \"results\", type_=\"foreignkey\")\n    op.create_foreign_key(\n        _FK, \"results\", \"checks\", [\"check_id\"], [\"id\"], ondelete=\"CASCADE\"\n    )\n\n\ndef downgrade() -> None:\n    op.drop_constraint(_FK, \"results\", type_=\"foreignkey\")\n    op.create_foreign_key(_FK, \"results\", \"checks\", [\"check_id\"], [\"id\"])\n"
}

def test_delete_returns_204_then_404(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    sid = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id)).json()["id"]
    deleted = client.delete(f"/api/v1/suites/{sid}")
    assert deleted.status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"/api/v1/suites/{sid}").status_code == 404


def test_delete_cascades_to_checks(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    conn = _connection(db_session)
    sid = client.post("/api/v1/suites", json=_payload(conn.id)).json()["id"]
    # attach a check directly (check CRUD lands in the next PR)
    db_session.add(
        Check(suite_id=uuid.UUID(sid), name="row_count", expectation_type="expect_table_row_count")
    )
    db_session.commit()

    deleted = client.delete(f"/api/v1/suites/{sid}")
    assert deleted.status_code == 204
    remaining = db_session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == uuid.UUID(sid))).all()
    assert remaining == []  # cascade removed the child check


# ───────────────────────── access enforcement (PR-E2) ──────────────
def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
    try:
        yield TestClient(app)
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def _connection(db_session: Any) -> Connection:
    """Insert a connection (with its own owner) for suites to bind to."""
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email="owner@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "ab12345.eu-west-1"},
        secret_ref="kv-sf",
        created_by=owner.id,

286:**Current week:** **Week 7 of 8 — Deployment, hardening & docs — IN PROGRESS; DataQ v1 is now DEPLOYED TO AZURE and reachable** (Weeks 1–6 complete, all exit gates met). **Cloud deploy (2026-06-28):** the in-repo Terraform (`deploy/terraform/azure/`, ADR 0024) stood up the app stack into `dataq-rg` — `dataq-app-{api,worker}` + `dataq-app-migrate` job (GHCR slim image, ADR 0025) on the **shared `dataq-cae`** Container Apps env, `dataq-app-redis` (password-auth), Key Vault (UAMI) + App Insights + Log Analytics, and **`dataq-app-web`** Static Web App with the api **linked as same-origin `/api` backend**. The app's DB is a distinct **`dataq`** database + least-priv **`dataq_app`** role on the **shared `dataq-pg-wus3-*`** server (1-of-each free/trial cap → env + Postgres shared with the harness, neutral-named `purpose=dataq-shared`; harness Postgres backed-up→recreated→restored). Azure AD **SSO app registrations** (API + SPA) created in TF + wired; migrate job ran `alembic upgrade head`; API healthy (401 = auth-enforced), SPA + deep-links 200, GitHub OIDC secrets/vars + `production` env set. Fixed **#393** (opencensus AzureLogHandler `lock=None` on Py3.13) en route. **GHCR package→repo connect done** (Actions-access grant → CI's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push) and the **Deploy workflow validated end-to-end** (#403 fixed the migrate-command + frontend-pnpm bugs #401/#402; build→push→`alembic upgrade head`→ACA roll + SWA deploy all green on `v6`). **Post-deploy hardening (2026-06-28):** two production bugs surfaced and fixed — **#405** (Celery beat crashed on startup: the embedded `worker -B` beat re-nulled `self.lock` inside the opencensus `AzureLogHandler.createLock` fork on Python 3.13, silently killing ALL periodic tasks — orchestration polling, scheduled-suite dispatch, gap recovery, and sample-failure purge; fixed by making `createLock` idempotent in `backend/app/core/logging.py` + a network-free regression test; **#407** merged) and **#406** (deployed app couldn't read Key Vault: `AzureKeyVaultStore` called `DefaultAzureCredential()` with no args but the api+worker container runs a USER-assigned managed identity and `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` was unset — blocked connection tests, suite runs, AND orchestration polling; fixed by adding `AZURE_CLIENT_ID = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.client_id` to `local.app_env` in `deploy/terraform/azure/containerapps.tf`; **#408** merged). Backend image `:v7` built+pushed from main (with #405+#406); api+worker rolled to v7; App Insights re-enabled on the worker (the #405 mitigation of temporarily dropping `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` on the worker is reverted) — landed as **#409** (`image_tag` default v4→v7). **Orchestration polling is now live end-to-end** — beat starts clean (zero NoneType crashes) with App Insights on, api healthy (401, auth-enforced), ADF+Airflow connections polling via the 10-min beat fallback, Key Vault secrets read successfully. **Post-deploy feature batch (2026-06-29, all merged; prod image `:v7`→`:v10`):** Slack + email alert publishers behind the `ResultPublisher` seam (#413, `:v8`), column-aware failing-sample redaction (#417) + the #383/#384/#395/#423 hardening batch (`:v9`, bump #414), URL-encode DB password (#421/#395), always-alert operationally-failed runs (#419), alerting upsert race fix (#420/#384), per-run check outcome in the runs table (#425/#423), mypy gate over `backend/tests` (#418), and — **pulling ADR 0012 post-v1 Theme A forward — freshness & volume monitor-kinds end-to-end** (run engine #426 + authoring path & check-editor UI #437, `:v10`, bump #438). > AGENT

#539 is two distinct transients hitting the same job, so the fix is retry hardening in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` rather than chasing either root cause. Here's what I'd do:

## The two failure flavors

1. **`az containerapp update` → `KeyError: 'properties'`** (Deploys #1 and #2). The containerapp extension's `_polish_bad_errors` crashes when the ARM error response has no `properties` body — it masks the real error. The telling detail: the backend job runs the *identical* command on the same runner image and never fails, but the frontend update fires immediately after the backend job finished rolling api + worker + the migrate job on the same Container Apps environment. That points to a transient environment-busy conflict (409/429) whose error shape crashes the extension — not a version problem. Manual retry succeeded instantly all three times, confirming it's timing.
2. **Docker Hub 502 pulling `node:22-alpine`** (Deploy #3) — upstream registry blip before the image was even pushed.

## The fix (one small `ci:` PR, `Fixes #539`)

**Retry both flaky steps with a plain bash loop** — no third-party retry action (keeps the supply-chain surface flat, per rule 38 posture):

- **`Deploy frontend` step:** 3 attempts with 30/60s backoff; on final failure, rerun once with `--debug` so the masked ARM error actually lands in the log, then exit 1. After success, verify honestly: poll `az containerapp show --query properties.template.containers[0].image` until it equals the pushed tag — that also catches the case where the extension crashes *rendering a success*.
- **`Build + push frontend image` step:** same 3-attempt loop around the build command — Docker Hub blips resolve in seconds, and this also absorbs anonymous-pull rate-limit 429s, which look identical on shared runners.
- Optional third leg, cheap insurance: a short `sleep 30` or an explicit environment-provisioning-state wait between the backend job's last roll and the frontend update, since the conflict theory says the env is still settling. The retry loop already covers it, so I'd only add this if the KeyError recurs *with* retries.

**What I'd deliberately not do:** swap the base image to a Docker Hub mirror (supply-chain change for a once-off 502), pin a different containerapp extension version (backend's success in the same runs rules out version drift), or move to `nick-fields/retry` (new third-party action for something bash does in five lines).

Two notes from the incidents worth folding into the same PR: apply the identical retry+verify treatment to the **backend** `az containerapp update` steps too (they've been lucky, not immune — same command, same environment), and keep the failure loud (the current behavior of failing the job is correct; we just want it to only fail after real retries, with the real error visible).

Want me to implement it? It's a ~30-line workflow change; I'd validate with a `workflow_dispatch` run, though the flake is intermittent so a green run proves non-breakage rather than the fix itself.

69	      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible

72	      # `az containerapp job start` only *starts* the execution and returns, so we
73	      # capture the execution name and poll it to a terminal state — the rollout
74	      # below must not begin until the migration has actually SUCCEEDED, and a
75	      # failed migration must abort the deploy (fail-closed) rather than roll the
76	      # apps onto an un-migrated schema.
77	      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success

81	          # --image override. Passing --image to `job start` replaces the
82	          # container template without the Terraform-configured command
83	          # (`sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"`), so the execution
84	          # falls back to the image's default CMD (uvicorn) and never migrates.
85	          # Updating the template preserves that command (mirrors the api/worker

87	          az containerapp job update \

91	          exec_name=$(az containerapp job start \
92	            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
93	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
94	            --query name -o tsv)
95	          echo "Started migration execution: $exec_name"
96	          # Poll to a terminal state. Besides the 15-min wall-clock cap, bound the
97	          # number of *consecutive* empty/unexpected statuses: a control-plane
98	          # hiccup or a CLI status-field rename would otherwise leave the loop
99	          # polling a status it never recognises until the full deadline, tying up
100	          # the prod concurrency group with no signal (#397). A recognised
101	          # in-progress status resets the counter; `|| true` keeps a transient
102	          # query failure a retry (counted as unknown) rather than a hard step
103	          # abort under `set -e`.
104	          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 900 ))  # 15-minute cap
105	          unknown=0
106	          unknown_max=18  # ~3 min of consecutive empty/unexpected status → abort
107	          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
108	            status=$(az containerapp job execution list \
109	              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
110	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
111	              --query "[?name=='$exec_name'].properties.status | [0]" -o tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
112	            echo "migration status: ${status:-<pending>} (unknown streak: $unknown)"
113	            case "$status" in
114	              Succeeded) echo "Migration succeeded."; exit 0 ;;
115	              Failed|Degraded|Stopped) echo "::error::Migration $status — aborting before app rollout."; exit 1 ;;
116	              Running|Processing|Pending) unknown=0 ;;
117	              *)
118	                unknown=$(( unknown + 1 ))
119	                if (( unknown >= unknown_max )); then
120	                  echo "::error::Migration status empty/unexpected ('${status:-<empty>}') $unknown times in a row — aborting before app rollout."
121	                  exit 1
122	                fi
123	                ;;
124	            esac
125	            sleep 10
126	          done
127	          echo "::error::Timed out waiting for migration to complete."; exit 1

  "content": "# Shared CI retry helper (#539) — source this, don't execute it.\n#\n# Both Deploy-workflow transients this covers are idempotent to re-run:\n#   - `az containerapp update/job update` crashing on a transient ARM error\n#     (the containerapp extension's `_polish_bad_errors` masks 409/429-style\n#     responses as `KeyError: 'properties'` — Deploys #1/#2, 2026-07-02)\n#   - registry blips during image build/push (Docker Hub 502 on the base-image\n#     pull — Deploy #3)\n#\n# Usage:  retry <cmd> [args…]        # 3 attempts, 30s/60s backoff\n# The command's exit code is propagated from the final attempt.\n\nretry() {\n  local attempt\n  for attempt in 1 2 3; do\n    \"$@\" && return 0\n    if (( attempt < 3 )); then\n      echo \"::warning::'$*' failed (attempt ${attempt}/3) — retrying in $(( attempt * 30 ))s (#539)\"\n      sleep $(( attempt * 30 ))\n    fi\n  done\n  echo \"::error::'$*' failed after 3 attempts (#539)\"\n  return 1\n}\n"

@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
+# Shared CI retry helper (#539) — source this, don't execute it.
+#
+# Both Deploy-workflow transients this covers are idempotent to re-run:
+#   - `az containerapp update/job update` crashing on a transient ARM error
+#     (the containerapp extension's `_polish_bad_errors` masks 409/429-style
+#     responses as `KeyError: 'properties'` — Deploys #1/#2, 2026-07-02)
+#   - registry blips during image build/push (Docker Hub 502 on the base-image
+#     pull — Deploy #3)
+#
+# Usage:  retry <cmd> [args…]        # 3 attempts, 30s/60s backoff
+# The command's exit code is propagated from the final attempt.
+
+retry() {
+  local attempt
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    "$@" && return 0
+    if (( attempt < 3 )); then
+      echo "::warning::'$*' failed (attempt ${attempt}/3) — retrying in $(( attempt * 30 ))s (#539)"
+      sleep $(( attempt * 30 ))
+    fi
+  done
+  echo "::error::'$*' failed after 3 attempts (#539)"
+  return 1
+}

> AGENT

Done — **Deploy #5 is fully green, including the frontend job's first CI success since the SWA→Container-App cutover.** All three apps (`api`, `worker`, `frontend`) verified on the new `a358ac60` image, `/healthz` ok, and no retries were needed — clean path.

The full story of what you asked for:

**#539 — fixed, and it wasn't what we thought.** The retry hardening (**#544**: shared `scripts/ci/retry.sh`, retry on all `az containerapp` mutations + both image builds, post-roll image verification, `--debug` last resort) went in first — and on its very first run, the `--debug` tail exposed the real cause: `az containerapp update --name ''`. **`vars.FRONTEND_APP_NAME` was never created** when the frontend moved off SWA (#509), so deploys #1/#2/#4 failed *deterministically* with the extension masking the ARM error as `KeyError: 'properties'`; only #3's Docker Hub 502 was a true transient. Resolution: the repo variable is now set, **#546** added a preflight step to both jobs that fails in seconds naming any unset var, the post-mortem is documented on #539, and Deploy #5 proved the whole chain. The retries stay — they cover the genuine transients and just demonstrated their diagnostic value.

**CodeQL alert — closed.** **#545** hoisted the `client.delete(...)` out of the assert in the #540 regression test (`py/side-effect-in-assert`); it was the only open code-scanning alert, and it auto-closes now that the fix is on `main`.

**Epic #176 — synced** at 36/40: the Azure-Monitor webhook group is ticked (collapsed to the one live factory, smoke 4m14s), Flows A/B/C and the deferred-smoke discharge are ticked, and the status header reflects the 2026-07-02 close-out. What's left on it: team onboarding and the optional Claude-Desktop client-side NL-selection check.

One standing reminder from earlier tonight: **rotate the Databricks PAT** (it hit App Insights logs before the #538 fix) — new PAT → KV secret `conn-unity-catalog-retail` → re-test the connection.

> AGENT

Here's the estimate, grounded in the actual config rather than guesswork.

**What runs on Databricks, and when.** The warehouse is the only compute: a **serverless SQL warehouse, size Small (12 DBU/hr), auto-stop 10 min**. The daily load is deliberately clustered: `flow_a_uc_reference` at 01:45 UTC, `flow_b_medallion` at 02:00, and the DataQ suite runs (Flow A-UC, silver/gold) trigger right behind each on the still-warm warehouse. That's one consolidated window of roughly **40–45 warehouse-minutes per day** (a few minutes of actual queries, the rest auto-stop idle tails).

**The math** (AWS serverless SQL list price ≈ $0.70/DBU):

| | Per day | 2 weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled window (~0.75 h × 12 DBU/h) | ~$6.30 | **~$88** |
| + ad-hoc touches (each stray connection test / dry-run / profiler call wakes the warehouse for a ~10-min tail ≈ $1.50–2) | +$1–3 | +$15–40 |
| **Realistic total** | **$7–9** | **≈ $90–130** |

Worth knowing: the trial credits burned fast because of the smoke/setup days — repeated manual runs, E2E, profiling kept the warehouse awake far more than the steady-state schedule will. Two quiet scheduled weeks are much cheaper than the past week was.

**If you want it cheaper before adding a card:** downsize the warehouse Small → 2X-Small (4 DBU/hr — the retail demo data won't notice) and drop `auto_stop_mins` from 10 to 5. Same schedules, same demo, and the two-week figure falls to roughly **$30–45**. Both are one-line API/UI changes I can make as soon as compute is billable again.

Storage and everything else are negligible here, and this is Databricks-only — Snowflake, ACA, and the rest of the Azure stack are unaffected either way.

So: adding a payment method costs you on the order of **$100 for the fortnight at current shape, or ~$35 trimmed**. If you'd rather not pay, say the word and I'll pause `flow_a_uc_reference` + `flow_b_medallion` so the dead UC lane doesn't spam failure alerts; Snowflake and flat-file lanes keep the demo alive.

> AGENT

Jobs are stopped and clean: both UC-touching DAGs paused, the stuck rotation-proof run is terminal (`failed`), and the last scheduled run before the credits died was green. No more failure-alert noise, and Snowflake/flat-file/event lanes keep running untouched.

On the payment question — short answer: **there's no self-serve one-time top-up for a trial workspace**, but you have three real alternatives:

1. **AWS Marketplace billing (closest to what you want).** This workspace is AWS-hosted, and you can subscribe to Databricks pay-as-you-go *through AWS Marketplace* — no card goes to Databricks; usage lands on your existing AWS bill, and any AWS credits you hold effectively prepay it. Functionally it's still PAYG, but there's no new payment relationship and you can cancel the subscription the moment the demo ends.
2. **Card PAYG, treated as one-time.** Usage-based with no minimum — at the paused-lane-resumed rate we estimated (~$35 trimmed / ~$100 untrimmed for the fortnight), you add the card, run two weeks, then downgrade/cancel. The "commitment" is only what you consume.
3. **Databricks Free Edition ($0, some rework).** A genuinely free serverless workspace with quota limits that would fit this demo. The cost is migration effort, not money: new workspace, recreate the UC catalog + retail data, new PATs, re-point the harness env + DataQ's two UC connections. Since `dataq_setup` and the harness scripts already exist, I could script most of that — realistically a couple of hours of work.

Two caveats: prepaid "commit" deals exist but only via Databricks sales (not worth it here), and billing options shift — worth a glance at the account console's upgrade page to confirm the Marketplace path is offered for your trial account (my knowledge has a cutoff).

My recommendation: AWS Marketplace if the no-card constraint is firm, otherwise the card + the two trim levers (warehouse → 2X-Small, auto-stop → 5 min — I'll apply both the moment compute is billable). If you pick Free Edition instead, I'll plan the migration. The paused DAGs resume with one API call either way.

## Databricks Free Edition Limitations

Databricks Free Edition is serverless-only with per-account quotas on compute, jobs, pipelines, model serving, Lakebase projects, and apps.

### Enterprise Admin Limitations

Free Edition accounts have several restrictions including:
- One workspace and one metastore per account.
- No access to the account console or account-level APIs.
- Authentication is limited to email OTP, Sign in with Google, and Sign in with Microsoft.

### Personal Access Tokens

While the search results provide information about how personal access tokens work with SQL warehouses and APIs, they don't contain specific limitations on PAT usage in Free Edition. The results show that BI Tools can connect to Databricks SQL warehouses such as Tableau or Power BI using scoped tokens, and tokens can include "sql" scopes for SQL warehouse access.

### Fair Usage Policy

If you exceed your quota, your workspace's compute resources will be shut down and unavailable for the rest of the day (and in extreme cases, the rest of the month).

For more detailed information about specific PAT limitations in Free Edition, you may want to consult the official Databricks documentation directly.

# Databricks Free Edition limitations - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn

Note

Databricks Free Edition is a no-cost offering and does not include guaranteed reliability, support, or service-level agreements. Free Edition accounts include many of the latest Databricks releases, but some features may be limited or unavailable. If you would like access to the full Databricks platform, you must create a new Databricks account by starting a [free trial](free-trial).

Databricks Free Edition is available at no cost to all qualified users. To keep it accessible to all, each account is subject to the Databricks fair usage policy.

If you exceed your quota, your workspace's compute resources will be shut down and unavailable for the rest of the day (and in extreme cases, the rest of the month). While your compute will be unavailable, your data and settings will not be deleted. You’ll be able to resume your work when the limit resets.

## Compute limitations

Free Edition users only have access to [serverless compute resources](../compute/serverless/). Custom compute configurations are not supported. Additionally, outbound internet access is restricted to a limited set of trusted domains.

Free Edition includes limited [serverless GPU compute](../machine-learning/ai-runtime/), available from the notebook compute selector and subject to available capacity.

| Resource | Limits |
| --- | --- |
| [Serverless compute for notebooks](../compute/serverless/notebooks) | Limited compute size and usage. |
| [SQL warehouses](../compute/sql-warehouse/) | One SQL warehouse, limited to a `2X-Small` cluster size. |
| [Jobs](../jobs/) | Max of 5 concurrent job tasks per account. |
| [Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines](../ldp/configure-pipeline) | One active pipeline per pipeline type. |
| [Model serving endpoints](../machine-learning/model-serving/) | - Limits on the number of active endpoints<br>- No GPU serving endpoints<br>- No [provisioned throughput](../machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/deploy-prov-throughput-foundation-model-apis)<br>- No custom models on GPU or batch inference<br>- Certain models not available |
| [AI Search endpoints](../ai-search/ai-search) | One AI Search endpoint, limited to one search unit. Additionally, Direct Vector Access in AI Search is not supported. |
| [Apps](../dev-tools/databricks-apps/) | Up to 3 Databricks Apps per account. Apps run for up to 24 hours after being started, updated, or redeployed. After that, the app is automatically stopped to help manage resource usage. You can restart the app at any time. |
| [Lakebase](../oltp/projects/) | One Lakebase project per account, with scale-to-zero compute. |

For a full list of serverless compute limitations, see [Serverless compute limitations](../compute/serverless/limitations).

## Unsupported features

The following features are not supported in Databricks Free Edition:

- R and Scala
- Custom workspace storage locations
- Online tables
- Clean rooms
- All legacy Databricks features
- [Knowledge Assistant](../agents/agent-bricks/knowledge-assistant)

## Administrative limitations

Free Edition accounts are meant for non-commercial use. Because of this, they have the following enterprise admin-related limits:

- One workspace and one metastore per account.
- No access to the account console or account-level APIs.
- No compliance enforcement, security customization, or private networking configurations.
- Authentication is limited to email OTP, Sign in with Google, and Sign in with Microsoft. No SSO or SCIM support.

## Additional limitations

- Databricks may delete Free Edition accounts that are inactive for a prolonged period.
- Free Edition accounts are not covered by the Databricks support policy or Service Level Agreement (SLA).
- Free Edition accounts may not be used for commercial purposes.
- Free Edition accounts cannot become Databricks Marketplace providers.
```

Yes — checked against the current Free Edition limitations doc (updated 2026-06-30), and **everything our UC lane does fits**, with one thing to verify at signup and one policy caveat. Here's the workload-by-workload mapping:

| Our workload | What it needs | Free Edition says | Fits? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flow_a_uc_reference` + `flow_b_medallion` DAGs | Airflow worker connects **in** via `databricks-sql-connector` to one SQL warehouse | One serverless SQL warehouse, **2X-Small** | ✅ — one warehouse is all we use, and 2X-Small is the downsize I recommended anyway |
| Flow B notebook step (RAW→Silver→Gold) | One job run at a time on serverless | Jobs capped at **5 concurrent tasks** | ✅ — we'd use 1 |
| DataQ UC connections (retail + qa): suite runs, dry-run, profiler | JDBC-style SQL over the same warehouse | Warehouse + workspace APIs available; only **account-level** APIs are off | ✅ — config-only change on DataQ's side (host/http_path/warehouse_id), no code |
| UC catalog/schemas/tables (retail model) | Create catalog + managed tables | One workspace + one metastore; managed storage only | ✅ — we don't use external storage; data arrives via INSERTs from the Airflow worker, so the restricted *outbound* internet doesn't touch us |
| Nightly usage volume | ~15–30 min of 2X-Small per day | Fair-use quota; compute pauses for the day if exceeded | ✅ — our footprint is tiny; heavy smoke days might hit the cap, scheduled load won't |
| R/Scala, custom compute, private networking | — | Unsupported | ✅ not used |

**The one thing to verify at signup:** the docs don't explicitly confirm **PAT support** — they restrict only account-level APIs and console auth methods (email OTP / Google / Microsoft), and workspace-level tooling is a headline use case, so PATs should work — but since every integration we have (Airflow env, DataQ secrets, my rotation recipe) authenticates with PATs, I'd create the account and mint a token as the very first step before committing to the migration. Two minutes to confirm.

**The policy caveat:** Free Edition is **non-commercial use only**, with no SLA and possible deletion after prolonged inactivity. For a portfolio/demo project that's fine; if DataQ's demo ever fronts anything commercial, it isn't.

**Migration effort if you go ahead** (~2–3 hours, mostly scripted already): new workspace → mint PATs → recreate the retail catalog/schemas + reseed (mockdata + the untracked notebook) → update `DATABRICKS_HOST`/`HTTP_PATH`/warehouse_id in harness tfvars + `secrets.sh` + the two Airflow ACA env entries → update the 3 KV secrets + the two DataQ connection configs → unpause the DAGs and re-run the Flow B verification.

Sources: [Databricks Free Edition limitations (Azure)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/getting-started/free-edition-limitations), [Databricks Free Edition limitations (AWS)](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/getting-started/free-edition-limitations)

Based on the search results, here's how to delete your Databricks account trial:

## Steps to Delete Your Databricks Account

**For Paid Accounts (AWS, GCP, Azure):**

In the account console sidebar, click Settings. Click the Manage your plan dropdown, then select Cancel plan. In the confirmation dialog, click Cancel plan.

**Before cancelling, Databricks recommends you:**
Terminate all compute resources in your Databricks workspaces. Delete all Unity Catalog metastores in the account. Go to each workspace and export any data or notebooks you want to import into a different account. Delete all Databricks workspaces in your account.

**Important:** Cancelling your Databricks plan is permanent and terminates your relationship with Databricks. You cannot reactivate a cancelled Databricks plan.

## After Cancelling the Plan

If you would like to fully delete your account, reach out to your account team for assistance or file a ticket at help.databricks.com. If you need to delete your Databricks account, reach out to your account team for assistance or file a ticket at help.databricks.com.

## For Free Edition Accounts

Currently, no self-serve option exists to delete a free edition account. You may try contacting help@databricks.com for assistance with removing the account.

## Important Note

In accordance with the Databricks terms of service, any customer content contained within workspaces tied to your subscription will be deleted within 30 days of cancellation.

Here's the current process — full deletion isn't self-serve, but you only need the self-serve half:

**Step 1 — Cancel the plan (self-serve, do this now):** go to the **account console** ([accounts.cloud.databricks.com](https://accounts.cloud.databricks.com)) → **Settings** → **Manage your plan** dropdown → **Cancel plan** → confirm. Prerequisites are already met on your side (compute gone, workspace deleted) — the one thing that can still block it is the **Unity Catalog metastore**: if cancel complains, delete the metastore first (account console → Catalog → delete metastore). Note the dialog's warning is accurate: cancellation is permanent, no reactivation.

**Step 2 — Actual account deletion (not self-serve):** Databricks only deletes the account record itself via a support ticket — file one at [help.databricks.com](https://help.databricks.com) (or email help@databricks.com) asking for account deletion, referencing the account email. Per their terms, all customer content tied to the subscription is auto-deleted **within 30 days of cancellation** regardless, so the ticket only matters if you want the login/registration itself erased.

**Practical take for our migration:** Step 1 is all that materially matters — $0 trial, no payment method, workspace gone, content auto-purges in 30 days. I wouldn't block the migration on the deletion ticket. And you can reuse **royarijit04@outlook.com** for the Free Edition signup even while the old account record lingers — Databricks shows an account picker at login when one email has multiple accounts.

So: hit **Cancel plan**, optionally file the deletion ticket, then sign up for [Free Edition](https://www.databricks.com/learn/free-edition) and send me the new workspace URL — I'll take it from the PAT gate onward.

**Migration complete — the UC lane is fully back on Databricks Free Edition at $0, end-to-end verified.** The final proof came straight from the prod DB: at **22:47:11Z** both trigger-bound DataQ suite runs (`airflow:flow_a_uc_reference:…` and `airflow:flow_b_medallion:…`) **succeeded** against the new warehouse — DAG load → success callback → DataQ ingest → auto-triggered GX suite run, the whole chain on the new workspace.

The full journey, as you sequenced it:

1. **Backup** — turned out minimal by design: no notebooks or Databricks jobs existed (Flow B is pure SQL from Airflow), so I dumped the 13 tables' column schemas + configs to `databricks/backup-2026-07-02/`; data was regenerable, DataQ's history lives in its own Postgres.
2. **Cancel + teardown** — nothing billable existed ($0 trial); you cancelled the plan and deleted the workspace; I cleaned the 8 dead resources out of the harness terraform state.
3. **Free Edition + PAT gate** — new workspace `dbc-4492dde4-090c`, CLI OAuth profile `dataq-free`, and the decisive check passed: **Free Edition mints PATs**.
4. **Replicate** — 3 dedicated 90-day PATs → the 3 KV secrets; one Free Edition quirk handled: Default Storage rejects catalog creation via TF/API, so `dataq_retail` + 4 schemas went in **via SQL** then `terraform import` — the harness apply is now fully clean (grants included) and rolled both Airflow apps to the new host/path/token; both DataQ connections PATCHed and testing `{ok:true}`.
5. **Resume** — DAGs unpaused, reseed runs green (dims + raw→silver→gold rebuilt), schedules live again, and the trigger-bound DataQ runs above sealed the verification.

Worth remembering: the warehouse is the fixed 2X-Small with config locked (auto-stop stays 10 min — irrelevant at $0), the fair-use quota pauses compute for the *day* if a heavy smoke session blows through it, and the account is non-commercial-only. Everything — new host, PAT expiries (~2026-09-30), the SQL-not-TF catalog quirk, the CLI profile — is recorded in memory and the closed `DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_TODO.md`.

1	"""Flow B — medallion (bronze -> silver -> gold) in Unity Catalog. §3b.
2	
3	Bronze NDJSON the §2a mockdata Jobs drop in ADLS is loaded into UC `raw` (worker reads
4	with pandas, writes via the Databricks SQL warehouse — same path as the reference loads);
5	silver/gold are SQL transforms on the warehouse. Implemented on the **serverless SQL
6	warehouse** rather than a PySpark job cluster: the trial workspace's reliable compute is
7	serverless, and reading ADLS from the warehouse is avoided by loading raw in the worker
8	(no UC storage credential for ADLS — that needs a role assignment the harness SP can't make).
9	
10	Pure ETL — DataQ discovers this run by polling the Airflow REST API, not via any push.
11	
12	Required env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,
13	DATABRICKS_HOST/TOKEN/HTTP_PATH, UC_CATALOG.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import os
19	
20	import pendulum
21	from _harness import load_to_uc, read_feed, run_uc_sql
22	from airflow import DAG
23	from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
24	from dataq_airflow_callback import on_dataq_failure, on_dataq_success
25	
26	CATALOG = os.environ.get("UC_CATALOG", "dataq_retail")
27	
28	
29	def _bronze(**_: object) -> None:
30	    """Load the raw NDJSON bronze sources into UC raw.* (schema-on-read)."""
31	    for feed in ("sales_events", "feedback"):
32	        df = read_feed(f"databricks_medallion/bronze/{feed}", "json")
33	        if not df.empty:
34	            load_to_uc(df, CATALOG, "raw", feed)
35	
36	
37	def _silver(**_: object) -> None:
38	    """Clean + PII-redact (sha2 the feedback email — #226); dedup; project sales."""
39	    run_uc_sql(
40	        [
41	            f"""CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`feedback` AS
42	                SELECT feedback_id, customer_id, channel, rating, comment,
43	                       sha2(CAST(email AS STRING), 256) AS email, created_ts
44	                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`raw`.`feedback`
45	                QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY feedback_id ORDER BY created_ts) = 1""",
46	            f"""CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`sales` AS
47	                SELECT order_number, channel, store_id,
48	                       CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
49	                       to_date(event_ts) AS sale_date
50	                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`raw`.`sales_events`
51	                WHERE event_type = 'placed'""",
52	        ]
53	    )
54	
55	
56	def _gold(**_: object) -> None:
57	    """Daily revenue rollup — reconciles back to Snowflake order_total (ADR 0014)."""
58	    run_uc_sql(
59	        [
60	            f"""CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE `{CATALOG}`.`gold`.`daily_revenue` AS
61	                SELECT sale_date, channel,
62	                       SUM(amount) AS daily_revenue,
63	                       COUNT(DISTINCT order_number) AS orders
64	                FROM `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`sales`
65	                GROUP BY sale_date, channel""",
66	        ]
67	    )
68	
69	
70	with DAG(
71	    default_args={
72	        # Retry transient failures (serverless warehouse cold start) with backoff.
73	        "retries": 4,
74	        "retry_delay": pendulum.duration(seconds=30),
75	        "retry_exponential_backoff": True,
76	        "max_retry_delay": pendulum.duration(minutes=5),
77	    },
78	    dag_id="flow_b_medallion",
79	    description="DataQ harness Flow B — UC bronze->silver->gold medallion (SQL warehouse)",
80	    schedule="0 2 * * *",  # after the Flow A loads
81	    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz="UTC"),
82	    catchup=False,
83	    # Notify DataQ on every run completion (success + failure); success fires the
84	    # bound suite. Fail-safe — a callback error never affects the DAG run.
85	    on_success_callback=on_dataq_success,
86	    on_failure_callback=on_dataq_failure,
87	    tags=["dataq-harness", "flow-b", "medallion"],
88	):
89	    bronze = PythonOperator(task_id="bronze_raw_load", python_callable=_bronze)
90	    silver = PythonOperator(task_id="silver_clean_pii", python_callable=_silver)
91	    gold = PythonOperator(task_id="gold_daily_revenue", python_callable=_gold)
92	    bronze >> silver >> gold
93

# mockdata image — runs as the Container Apps Job (cron) that produces files into
# the ADLS landing zone (§2a "file creation" layer). Same Python runtime as DataQ (3.13).
#
# Build (from harness root):  docker build -t mockdata:latest .
# Local smoke:                docker run --rm -v "$PWD/out:/data/out" -v "$PWD/state:/data/state" \
#                               mockdata:latest init --out /data/out --state /data/state
# Job invocation (per feed):  ... tick --feed inventory --out adls://<acct>/landing --state adls://<acct>/landing/state

FROM python:3.13-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Deps first for layer caching. pyarrow/pandas wheels are prebuilt for slim.
COPY mockdata/requirements.txt mockdata/requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r mockdata/requirements.txt

# Once built+pushed to the registry, set Terraform's `airflow_image` to this

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/harness-requirements.txt

COPY airflow/dags/ /opt/airflow/dags/

COPY airflow/webserver_config.py /opt/airflow/webserver_config.py

INCREMENTAL on purpose, twice over:\n\n    - `ai_analyze_sentiment` spends model-serving quota per row (Free Edition\n      fair-use pauses compute for the DAY when exhausted), so only rows not\n      already scored are sent to the model — a re-run scores nothing.\n    - MERGE (not CREATE OR REPLACE like the other gold step): rebuilding would\n      re-score the whole history every night for identical output.\n\n    `sentiment` is the AI verdict (positive|negative|neutral|mixed); `rating`\n    rides along so DataQ can cross-check the model against the 1–5 stars.\n    \"\"\"\n    run_uc_sql(\n        [\n            f\"\"\"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `{CATALOG}`.`gold`.`feedback_sentiment` (\n                    feedback_id STRING,\n                    customer_id STRING,\n                    channel STRING,\n                    rating BIGINT,\n                    sentiment STRING,\n                    created_ts STRING,\n                    scored_at TIMESTAMP)\"\"\",\n            f\"\"\"MERGE INTO `{CATALOG}`.`gold`.`feedback_sentiment` t\n                USING (\n                    SELECT s.feedback_id, s.customer_id, s.channel, s.rating,\n                           ai_analyze_sentiment(s.comment) AS sentiment,\n                           s.created_ts, current_timestamp() AS scored_at\n                    FROM `{CATALOG}`.`silver`.`feedback` s\n                    LEFT ANTI JOIN `{CATALOG}`.`gold`.`feedback_sentiment` g\n                        ON s.feedback_id = g.feedback_id\n                ) n\n                ON t.feedback_id = n.feedback_id\n                WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *\"\"\",\n        ]\n    )"

1:"""Resolve a suite's datasource-shaped target to the runner's (table, schema, catalog).
2-
3-A suite's `target` (#215) is a small JSONB document shaped like the column
4:profiler request (``table`` / ``schema`` / ``catalog`` / ``path`` /
5-``file_format``), datasource-typed. The `CheckRunner` interface is *table-shaped*
6-— for a flat-file datasource the file path rides the ``table`` argument
7-(``flatfile.py``) — so every datasource resolves to the same triple the worker
8-hands to ``run_service.execute_run`` and ``build_check_runner``:
9-
10-    snowflake      → table (+ schema)
11:    unity_catalog  → table (+ schema) + catalog        (catalog.schema.table)
12:    adls_gen2 / s3 → path  (carried as `table`; schema/catalog unused)
13-
14-A flat-file target can instead be a **batch** spec — files arrive in batches
15-(``orders_2026-06-01.csv`` …) and a run targets one of them: ``pattern`` (a regex
16-whose first capture group is the batch key) + ``strategy`` (``latest`` /
17-``specific``, with ``batch`` for ``specific``) + an optional ``prefix`` to list
18-under. The concrete path can only be known by *listing the store*, so it's
19-resolved at run time (`materialize_path`), not at save time.
20-
21-Resolution is two-phase so write-time validation stays pure (no network, no GX):
22-
--
70-class ResolvedTarget:
71-    """The runner inputs a suite resolves to. ``table`` carries the file path for
72:    flat-file datasources; ``catalog`` is set only for Unity Catalog. ``batch`` is
73-    set only for a flat-file *batch* target, in which case ``table`` is empty until
74-    `materialize_path` lists the store and resolves the concrete path."""
75-
76-    table: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PollIngestResult:
    pipeline_runs: list[PipelineRun] = field(default_factory=list)
    triggered_runs: list[Run] = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped: int = 0


def ingest_polled_runs(
    session: Session,
    *,
    provider_impl: OrchestrationProvider,
    connection: Connection,
    updates: list[RunUpdate],
    skip_updated_since: datetime,
) -> PollIngestResult:
    """Persist the runs a poll returned for one orchestrator connection.

    Records **every status** for the monitor view (#490), but stays the
    **trigger-on-success** channel (ADR 0004): only a ``succeeded`` run triggers a
    suite — failures/running are recorded, never triggered (mirrors `ingest_event`).
    Poll data is already authoritative, so there is no REST enrichment.

    The ``skip_updated_since`` churn-optimisation skips a run we already recorded
    inside this window — but **only when the existing row is already terminal**
    (succeeded/failed/cancelled). A non-terminal row (queued/running) must always
    be re-processed: now that the poll records non-terminal states (#490), skipping
    it on time alone would drop a later ``running → succeeded`` transition — losing
    both the monitor update *and* the trigger. The connection is known (we polled
    it), so no resolve.
    """
    provider = provider_impl.provider
    pipeline_runs: list[PipelineRun] = []
    triggered: list[Run] = []
    skipped = 0
    for update in updates:
        existing = session.execute(
            select(PipelineRun.status, PipelineRun.last_updated_at).where(
                PipelineRun.provider == provider,
                PipelineRun.provider_run_id == update.provider_run_id,
            )
        ).first()
        if (
            existing is not None
            and existing.status in _TERMINAL_PIPELINE_STATUSES
            and existing.last_updated_at >= skip_updated_since
        ):
            skipped += 1
            continue
        pipeline_runs.append(
            _upsert_pipeline_run(session, provider=provider, connection=connection, update=update)
```

15	- **§2a recurring cadence** — tick mode + persisted state (master pools + climbing id counters + open-shipment registry → consistency across ticks). Shared `storage.py` `Store` seam (`LocalStore`/`AdlsStore` via `make_store`) backs **both** `--state` and `--out`; both accept `adls://<acct>/<fs>[/<prefix>]`. Repo-root `Dockerfile` (3.13-slim + pandas/pyarrow/azure) → runs as the file-creation engine. **Cadence decisions:** file creation = **Container Apps Job (cron)** running the image (source-system simulator, upstream); load+trigger = **ADF/Airflow** with a *mix* of file-landing-event (orders/tracking) and scheduled-time (inventory/feedback) triggers → DataQ. So §1 Terraform now also provisions a shared **Container Apps Environment** (hosts Airflow scheduler+webserver *and* the mockdata Job) + a **container registry** (both images) + **Postgres** (Airflow metadata). > AGENT

**Done — the feedback sentiment layer now exists end-to-end, and the full chain is verified green.** The trigger-bound run (`67cd44f4`) passed **4/4 checks** with 0% unexpected rows.

To answer your original question honestly: it wasn't in any tracker — no mention of sentiment analysis in `HARNESS_TODO` (since retired), the roadmap, docs, or DAGs; feedback data previously dead-ended at silver. So I built it as a proper Flow B extension:

**The pipeline** (`flow_b_medallion`, now 4 stages): bronze → silver → gold revenue → **`gold_feedback_sentiment`** — a new task that scores `silver.feedback.comment` with Databricks' `ai_analyze_sentiment()` (verified working on Free Edition first). It's deliberately **incremental** (MERGE with an anti-join, only unscored rows hit the model) — both to avoid re-burning the fair-use quota nightly and to avoid re-scoring identical history. Current state of `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment`: **80 comments — 41 positive, 31 negative, 8 mixed**, with `rating` alongside so the AI verdict can be cross-checked against the stars. Shipped as Airflow image `callback-2` (DAGs are baked in), rolled via terraform.

**The DataQ side**: new suite **"Feedback Sentiment — UC gold"** (owned by Olivia) with 4 checks — `sentiment` not-null, `sentiment` in {positive, negative, neutral, mixed}, `rating` between 1–5, and volume ≥ 1 — plus a **trigger binding** on `(airflow, flow_b_medallion, dev)`. That makes it the second suite bound to Flow B (the dedup index is per-suite, so both fire), and tonight's run proved it: DAG success → callback/poll ingest → auto-triggered suite run → **succeeded, all checks pass**.

It's a nice demo arc now: an *AI-derived* gold table with DQ guardrails on the model's output shape — if the model starts emitting junk labels or the feedback feed stalls, DataQ alerts. Docs and memory are updated (harness README documents the new stage; the stale `HARNESS_TODO` pointer in memory is fixed).

One design note: the "in allowed set" check treats `neutral` as valid but none appeared in this batch — if you'd like a *distribution* guard (e.g., alert when negative share spikes above X%), that's a custom-SQL check away; say the word.

Yes — checked against the current Free Edition limitations doc (updated 2026-06-30), and **everything our UC lane does fits**, with one thing to verify at signup and one policy caveat. Here's the workload-by-workload mapping:

| Our workload | What it needs | Free Edition says | Fits? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flow_a_uc_reference` + `flow_b_medallion` DAGs | Airflow worker connects **in** via `databricks-sql-connector` to one SQL warehouse | One serverless SQL warehouse, **2X-Small** | ✅ — one warehouse is all we use, and 2X-Small is the downsize I recommended anyway |
| Flow B notebook step (RAW→Silver→Gold) | One job run at a time on serverless | Jobs capped at **5 concurrent tasks** | ✅ — we'd use 1 |
| DataQ UC connections (retail + qa): suite runs, dry-run, profiler | JDBC-style SQL over the same warehouse | Warehouse + workspace APIs available; only **account-level** APIs are off | ✅ — config-only change on DataQ's side (host/http_path/warehouse_id), no code |
| UC catalog/schemas/tables (retail model) | Create catalog + managed tables | One workspace + one metastore; managed storage only | ✅ — we don't use external storage; data arrives via INSERTs from the Airflow worker, so the restricted *outbound* internet doesn't touch us |
| Nightly usage volume | ~15–30 min of 2X-Small per day | Fair-use quota; compute pauses for the day if exceeded | ✅ — our footprint is tiny; heavy smoke days might hit the cap, scheduled load won't |
| R/Scala, custom compute, private networking | — | Unsupported | ✅ not used |

**The one thing to verify at signup:** the docs don't explicitly confirm **PAT support** — they restrict only account-level APIs and console auth methods (email OTP / Google / Microsoft), and workspace-level tooling is a headline use case, so PATs should work — but since every integration we have (Airflow env, DataQ secrets, my rotation recipe) authenticates with PATs, I'd create the account and mint a token as the very first step before committing to the migration. Two minutes to confirm.

**The policy caveat:** Free Edition is **non-commercial use only**, with no SLA and possible deletion after prolonged inactivity. For a portfolio/demo project that's fine; if DataQ's demo ever fronts anything commercial, it isn't.

**Migration effort if you go ahead** (~2–3 hours, mostly scripted already): new workspace → mint PATs → recreate the retail catalog/schemas + reseed (mockdata + the untracked notebook) → update `DATABRICKS_HOST`/`HTTP_PATH`/warehouse_id in harness tfvars + `secrets.sh` + the two Airflow ACA env entries → update the 3 KV secrets + the two DataQ connection configs → unpause the DAGs and re-run the Flow B verification.

Sources: [Databricks Free Edition limitations (Azure)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/getting-started/free-edition-limitations), [Databricks Free Edition limitations (AWS)](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/getting-started/free-edition-limitations)

> AGENT

**Migration complete — the UC lane is fully back on Databricks Free Edition at $0, end-to-end verified.** The final proof came straight from the prod DB: at **22:47:11Z** both trigger-bound DataQ suite runs (`airflow:flow_a_uc_reference:…` and `airflow:flow_b_medallion:…`) **succeeded** against the new warehouse — DAG load → success callback → DataQ ingest → auto-triggered GX suite run, the whole chain on the new workspace.

The full journey, as you sequenced it:

1. **Backup** — turned out minimal by design: no notebooks or Databricks jobs existed (Flow B is pure SQL from Airflow), so I dumped the 13 tables' column schemas + configs to `databricks/backup-2026-07-02/`; data was regenerable, DataQ's history lives in its own Postgres.
2. **Cancel + teardown** — nothing billable existed ($0 trial); you cancelled the plan and deleted the workspace; I cleaned the 8 dead resources out of the harness terraform state.
3. **Free Edition + PAT gate** — new workspace `dbc-4492dde4-090c`, CLI OAuth profile `dataq-free`, and the decisive check passed: **Free Edition mints PATs**.
4. **Replicate** — 3 dedicated 90-day PATs → the 3 KV secrets; one Free Edition quirk handled: Default Storage rejects catalog creation via TF/API, so `dataq_retail` + 4 schemas went in **via SQL** then `terraform import` — the harness apply is now fully clean (grants included) and rolled both Airflow apps to the new host/path/token; both DataQ connections PATCHed and testing `{ok:true}`.
5. **Resume** — DAGs unpaused, reseed runs green (dims + raw→silver→gold rebuilt), schedules live again, and the trigger-bound DataQ runs above sealed the verification.

Worth remembering: the warehouse is the fixed 2X-Small with config locked (auto-stop stays 10 min — irrelevant at $0), the fair-use quota pauses compute for the *day* if a heavy smoke session blows through it, and the account is non-commercial-only. Everything — new host, PAT expiries (~2026-09-30), the SQL-not-TF catalog quirk, the CLI profile — is recorded in memory and the closed `DATABRICKS_MIGRATION_TODO.md`.

3-A suite's `target` (#215) is a small JSONB document shaped like the column
4:profiler request (``table`` / ``schema`` / ``catalog`` / ``path`` /
5-``file_format``), datasource-typed. The `CheckRunner` interface is *table-shaped*
6-— for a flat-file datasource the file path rides the ``table`` argument
7-(``flatfile.py``) — so every datasource resolves to the same triple the worker
8-hands to ``run_service.execute_run`` and ``build_check_runner``:
9-
10-    snowflake      → table (+ schema)
11:    unity_catalog  → table (+ schema) + catalog        (catalog.schema.table)
12:    adls_gen2 / s3 → path  (carried as `table`; schema/catalog unused)
13-
14-A flat-file target can instead be a **batch** spec — files arrive in batches
15-(``orders_2026-06-01.csv`` …) and a run targets one of them: ``pattern`` (a regex
16-whose first capture group is the batch key) + ``strategy`` (``latest`` /
17-``specific``, with ``batch`` for ``specific``) + an optional ``prefix`` to list
18-under. The concrete path can only be known by *listing the store*, so it's
19-resolved at run time (`materialize_path`), not at save time.
20-
21-Resolution is two-phase so write-time validation stays pure (no network, no GX):

38-## Known limitations (v1)
39-
40-- **GX-only** check engine (Databricks DQX deferred to v1.1); batch-oriented (not
41-  streaming).
42-- **Single tenant**, suite-level access sharing; workspace-admin is a config allowlist.
43-- Interactive **datasource browsing** (container browser, 3-level UC catalog picker) is
44-  deferred — you specify targets explicitly. JSON flat files deferred (CSV/Parquet in v1).

47-## FAQ
48-
49-**Is ADF/Airflow a datasource?** No — they're orchestration providers DataQ monitors and
50-can trigger from. You never write checks against them. See **[Concepts](concepts.md)**.
51-
52-**Do I need Azure to run it locally?** No — local dev uses a dev-bypass auth and
53-docker-compose. Azure is one deployment target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013).

55-**Where do failed-row samples go?** Stored with the result, **PII-redacted**, and purged
56-after a retention window — never written to logs.

59-/ Copilot / Cursor), Azure-AD authenticated. See the README's MCP section.

37-### Run DataQ — prebuilt images (recommended)
38-
39-Evaluate or self-host in ~5 minutes: **no source checkout, no Azure tenant.** Just Docker.
40-
41-```bash
42-curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/main/docker-compose.ghcr.yml
43-docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up
44-```
45-
46-Open **<http://localhost:3000>** — the stack comes up migrated and seeded with demo data, on **dev-bypass auth** (every request is a fixed demo user; no sign-in). API + Swagger at `http://localhost:8000/docs`. Images are pulled from GHCR and are **multi-arch** (amd64 + arm64), so Apple-Silicon runs native. Ports bind to `127.0.0.1` only. To pin a release instead of the moving tags: `DATAQ_BACKEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z DATAQ_FRONTEND_TAG=vX.Y.Z docker compose -f docker-compose.ghcr.yml up`.
47-
48-> Self-hosting with **your own** Azure AD? The published frontend is **one generic image** — the compose eval runs it with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=bypass` (auth off). For real SSO, **no rebuild**: run that same image with `DATAQ_AUTH_MODE=oidc` + `DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY` / `DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `DATAQ_AUTH_API_SCOPE` (auth config is injected at runtime, ADR 0028), and run the backend with `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS` off. See [Getting started](https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/getting-started/).

62:## MCP (AI assistant access)
63-
64:DataQ exposes 8 curated MCP tools at `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) — `list_suites`, `get_suite_results`, `get_health_score`, `get_adf_pipeline_status`, `trigger_suite_run`, `get_run_status`, `create_check`, `profile_column`. The endpoint is **Azure AD–protected**: present the same bearer token the web UI uses (validated against the same tenant / audience / scope). Without Azure auth configured the endpoint is only mounted in local dev-bypass mode — never unauthenticated in a deployed environment (ADR [0008](docs/adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).
65-
66:Point any MCP client at `https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp` with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

224:- [x] ✅ Run history retention policy — configurable purge of results older than N days — **PII-minimisation sweep** (not a row delete: ADR 0012 wants `metric_value` trends to outlive samples). Daily Celery-beat `purge_sample_failures` → `run_service.purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubs `sample_failures` (the only potentially-PII result column) to SQL NULL + stamps `sample_failures_purged_at` on results older than the configurable `sample_failures_retention_days` (default 30). Honoured the pre-built seam (the column + setting + the three "retention sweep" comments existed with no writer). Targets only real sample *objects* via `jsonb_typeof` (the JSONB column stores Python `None` as JSON `'null'`, so `IS NOT NULL` over-matches every passing/errored row); naturally idempotent (scrubbed → SQL NULL → excluded); `retention_days <= 0` disables. 6 DB-backed sweep tests + 1 task-wiring unit test. **(A8)**
299:**Exit gate:** Production-ready v1 deployed to Azure, CI/CD live, team onboarded.
322:- [x] ✅ **Post-deploy bug: Celery beat crash on startup (closes [#405](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/405))** — the embedded `worker -B` beat process was re-nulling `self.lock` inside `AzureLogHandler.createLock()` on Python 3.13 (a recurrence of the #393 lock issue in the beat fork), silently killing **all** periodic tasks — orchestration polling (ADF + Airflow), scheduled-suite dispatch, gap recovery, and the sample-failure purge. Fix: override `createLock` in `backend/app/core/logging.py` to be idempotent (only ever create a missing lock, never null/swap one) + a network-free regression test in `backend/tests/core/test_logging.py`. — **[#407](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/407)**

Manual/probe/schedule markers legitimately repeat (positive predicate degrades safely). Follow-up [#457](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/457) (drift guard for a future provider).
362	- [x] ✅ **Stuck-run reaper** — fixed in [#458](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/458) (closes [#309](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/309)): a beat janitor fails runs left non-terminal past `STUCK_RUN_THRESHOLD_MINUTES` (default 60); **fails** rather than re-dispatches (a null `celery_task_id` doesn't prove the task wasn't published), and deliberately doesn't alert (an over-threshold `running` run is indistinguishable from slow-but-alive — avoids an irreversible false alarm).

258	## Operational notes
259	
260	- **Restart dependent Container Apps after a shared-Postgres delete/recreate** —
261	  the DB host is injected as a start-time secret snapshot, so every dependent
262	  revision must be restarted or it keeps resolving the old/dead host.
263	- The shared RG / Container Apps env / Postgres server are **reused, never
264	  destroyed** (free/trial caps one of each; shared with the harness — ADR 0024).
265	- `key_vault_purge_protection` is off during bring-up (so a destroy/re-apply can
266	  reuse the vault name); set it **true** for a hardened prod (irreversible).
267	- **Workspace-admins are superusers over every suite** ([ADR 0027](../docs/adr/0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md) / #482):
268	  anyone in `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` can read **all** suites' results — including
269	  failing-row samples (`results.sample_failures`), the one place PII/PHI lands —
270	  and manage/delete any suite. **Keep the allowlist minimal.** For a **PHI / regulated
271	  deployment**, treat the data-access audit trail (G1 / #431 in
```

While CI finishes (I'll merge #549 automatically once it's green and the docs review comes back), here's the Claude Desktop walkthrough you asked for.

## Bookkeeping done

- **Team onboarding** — marked ✅ (discharged via the six demo users cross-shared at every ADR-0027 tier), and **KV purge-protection** — decision recorded as *deliberately left off* in [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md), with the revisit condition. Both landed in [PR #549](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/549) along with reconciling the checklist rows the live smoke had only flipped in the headline (Azure-Monitor section now 5/5 ✅, live run paths ✅). **Week 7 closes at 39/40**; epic #176 is synced. The one open row is exactly the thing below.

## Claude Desktop setup — what needs to happen

**What this check actually validates:** the protocol level already passed (I ran the 4-query smoke directly against live `/mcp` with a real token — auth, tool listing, tool calls all green). The only untested sliver is whether **Claude Desktop's own model picks the right DataQ tool from natural language** — i.e., whether the LLM-facing tool descriptions work in a real client. That's it; it's a ~10-minute check.

**Step 1 — Get a bearer token.** DataQ's `/mcp` accepts the same Azure AD token the web UI uses. Easiest manual path: sign into the app at `https://dataq-app-frontend.purplefield-f7322a1b.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io` (e.g., as Olivia), open browser DevTools → Application → **Session Storage** → the `oidc.user:…` key → copy the `access_token` value. (Alternatively I can mint one from the captured live-smoke session and write it straight into the config file without it ever appearing on screen — say the word.)

**Step 2 — Configure Claude Desktop.** Edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` and add the server per the README's MCP section:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dataq": {
      "url": "https://dataq-app-frontend.purplefield-f7322a1b.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <paste the token>" }
    }
  }
}
```

If your Desktop version doesn't accept direct `url` entries (older builds are stdio-only), use the `mcp-remote` bridge instead — same file:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dataq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://dataq-app-frontend.purplefield-f7322a1b.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp",
        "--header", "Authorization: Bearer <paste the token>"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop. You should see **dataq** under the tools/connectors icon with 8 tools listed.

**Step 3 — Run the 4 canonical queries** (from the roadmap; each should select a different tool without you naming it):

1. *"What data quality checks failed today?"* → should call `get_suite_results` / `list_suites`
2. *"Run the Retail Orders suite"* → `trigger_suite_run` (then *"is it done?"* → `get_run_status`)
3. *"Why did the ADF pipeline fail?"* → `get_adf_pipeline_status`
4. *"Add a not-null check on order_number in the Retail Orders suite"* → `create_check`

Pass = right tool chosen each time and a sensible answer comes back. If a query picks the wrong tool, that's a tool-*description* fix in `backend/app/mcp/` — file an issue rather than tweaking live.

**Two caveats to expect:**
- **Token expiry (~1 hour).** The token is a static paste, so after it expires Desktop's dataq server starts erroring until you paste a fresh one and restart. This is the known v1 limitation — DataQ-issued API keys (ADR 0026 / #461) are the post-v1 fix that makes this a set-once config.
- Everything is scoped to the signed-in user's suite access — as Olivia you'll see her owned/shared suites, which is exactly the authz behaviour we want to observe.

I'll report back once CI is green and #549 is merged.

322	- [x] ✅ **Post-deploy bug: Celery beat crash on startup (closes [#405](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/405))** — the embedded `worker -B` beat process was re-nulling `self.lock` inside `AzureLogHandler.createLock()` on Python 3.13 (a recurrence of the #393 lock issue in the beat fork), silently killing **all** periodic tasks — orchestration polling (ADF + Airflow), scheduled-suite dispatch, gap recovery, and the sample-failure purge. Fix: override `createLock` in `backend/app/core/logging.py` to be idempotent (only ever create a missing lock, never null/swap one) + a network-free regression test in `backend/tests/core/test_logging.py`. — **[#407](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/407)**
323	- [x] ✅ **Post-deploy bug: deployed app couldn't read Key Vault (closes [#406](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/406))** — `AzureKeyVaultStore` called `DefaultAzureCredential()` with no args, but the api+worker containers run a USER-assigned managed identity and `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` was unset in the Container Apps env, so every `get_secret` call failed (`SecretNotFoundError` / `DefaultAzureCredential failed`). This blocked connection tests, suite runs, AND orchestration polling. Fix: add `AZURE_CLIENT_ID = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.client_id` to `local.app_env` in `deploy/terraform/azure/containerapps.tf` (shared by the api and worker). — **[#408](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/408)**
324	- [x] ✅ **Redeploy after post-deploy fixes — now at image `:v10`** — `image_tag` default tracks the live prod image: `:v7` (#405 beat-lock + #406 KV `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, [#409](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/409)) → `:v8` (Slack+email alerting #413) → `:v9` (column-aware redaction #417 + the #383/#384/#395/#423 hardening batch, [#414](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/414)) → **`:v10`** (freshness/volume monitors #426 + authoring UI #437 + runs-table outcome #425, [#438](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/438)). Each bumped in `deploy/terraform/azure/variables.tf`. Verified live: beat clean, api healthy (401, auth-enforced), orchestration polling reads KV secrets.
325	- [x] ✅ **Cloud-neutral cutover: frontend Static Web App → Container App (ADR [0028](adr/0028-cloud-neutral-image-runtime-config-generic-oidc.md) §5)** — the deployed frontend is now `dataq-app-frontend`, the **sole public surface**, running the one generic nginx image with runtime `DATAQ_AUTH_*` OIDC config (**MSAL retired** → generic oidc-client-ts; validated live as Olivia → dashboard). The **api moved to internal ingress** (reached only via the frontend proxy `/api` + `/mcp` + `/healthz`); the SWA is destroyed. Chain **[#509](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/509)** (cutover) → **[#510](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/510)** (`lifecycle ignore_changes` on container images so applies never roll prod back + on the api `identifier_uris` so applies never strip the token audience) → **[#511](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/511)** (three ACA gotchas: nginx must proxy **HTTP/1.1** or ACA 426s; api ingress **HTTP + `allow_insecure_connections`**; orphaned SWA-**EasyAuth** on the api disabled — 401'd everything post-SWA-destroy). Prod frontend `:v2`. Follow-up **[#512](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/512)** (multi-arch frontend QEMU build impractically slow/flaky) **fixed by [#518](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/518)** — `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` cross-build of the arch-neutral Vite build; frontend publish 45-min-stall → ~1min, native-arm64 `:latest` restored. AWS/GCP deploy IaC stays post-v1 ([#505](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/505)).

> AGENT

Checked and fixed — your config now works against the live server. Verified with the exact URL + token from the file: MCP `initialize` → `DataQ 3.4.2` (signed in as Olivia), and `tools/list` returns all **8 tools** (`list_suites, get_suite_results, get_health_score, get_adf_pipeline_status, trigger_suite_run, get_run_status, create_check, profile_column`).

Two corrections I made to [.vscode/mcp.json](.vscode/mcp.json):

1. **The URL was missing the `/mcp` path** — it pointed at the site root, so VS Code would have gotten the SPA's HTML instead of the MCP endpoint.
2. **Made it `/mcp/` with the trailing slash** — the mount 307-redirects `/mcp` → `/mcp/`, and many HTTP clients drop the `Authorization` header when following a redirect, which would show up as a confusing 401.

Also confirmed the safety angle: `.vscode/mcp.json` is **gitignored** (the `.vscode/*` rule), so the embedded bearer token can't be committed — consistent with the no-creds-in-tracked-files agreement.

Two things to know when you use it:

- **The token expires ~70 minutes from now.** After that VS Code will start getting 401s from the server — grab a fresh `access_token` from the web app's session storage (or ask me to refresh it into the file) and restart the server. Set-and-forget config arrives with ADR 0026 API keys post-v1.
- To connect in VS Code: `Cmd+Shift+P` → **MCP: List Servers** → `DataQ_MCP` → Start (or just open Copilot Chat in agent mode — it starts configured servers on demand). If it was already running from before my fix, restart it so it picks up the corrected URL.

This VS Code/Copilot connection is effectively the same client-side check as the Claude Desktop one — if you run the 4 canonical queries here ("what suites do I have?", "what failed today?", "run the Retail Orders suite", "why did the ADF pipeline fail?") and Copilot picks the right tools, I'd call the last Week-7 row done.

## MCP (AI assistant access)

DataQ exposes 8 curated MCP tools at `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) — `list_suites`, `get_suite_results`, `get_health_score`, `get_adf_pipeline_status`, `trigger_suite_run`, `get_run_status`, `create_check`, `profile_column`. The endpoint is **Azure AD–protected**: present the same bearer token the web UI uses (validated against the same tenant / audience / scope). Without Azure auth configured the endpoint is only mounted in local dev-bypass mode — never unauthenticated in a deployed environment (ADR [0008](docs/adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).

Point any MCP client at `https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp` with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

**Claude Desktop / Claude.ai** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) — and **GitHub Copilot** (`mcp.json`):

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dataq": {
      "url": "https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <AZURE_AD_ACCESS_TOKEN>" }
    }
  }
}
```

**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) uses the same `mcpServers` shape. Once configured, all 8 tools are available to natural-language queries (e.g. *"what failed in the orders suite today?"*, *"run the orders suite on DEV"*).
```

site_name: DataQ
site_description: >-
  DataQ — a single-tenant data-quality monitoring platform built on Great
  Expectations. User-friendly guides + developer references.
site_url: https://theurgicduke771.github.io/DataQ/
repo_url: https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ
repo_name: TheurgicDuke771/DataQ
edit_uri: edit/main/docs/

# The repo's docs/ is the source. Internal planning docs are excluded from the
# published site (below); ADRs are published as reference.
docs_dir: docs

theme:
  name: material
  palette:
    - scheme: default
      primary: indigo # matches the app's indigo brand
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/weather-night
        name: Switch to dark mode
    - scheme: slate
      primary: indigo
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/weather-sunny
        name: Switch to light mode
  features:
    - navigation.sections
    - navigation.top
    - navigation.instant
    - navigation.footer
    - toc.follow
    - search.suggest
    - search.highlight
    - content.code.copy

markdown_extensions:
  - admonition
  - attr_list
  - tables
  - toc:
      permalink: true
  - pymdownx.highlight
  - pymdownx.inlinehilite
  - pymdownx.snippets
  - pymdownx.superfences:
      custom_fences:
        - name: mermaid
          class: mermaid
          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format

# Plain-language modules first (audience: PMs / data engineers / SREs / QA /
# non-technical stakeholders), then developer references. Each module is short
# and links out to the in-repo source of truth rather than duplicating it.
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Guides:
      - Getting started: getting-started.md
      - Concepts: concepts.md
      - Datasources & checks: datasources-checks.md
      - Scheduling: scheduling.md
      - Orchestration: orchestration.md
      - Notifications & alerting: notifications.md
      - Best practices: best-practices.md
  - Reference:
      - Feature matrix: feature-matrix.md
      - Architecture: architecture.md
      - Observability & troubleshooting: observability.md
      - Runbook & FAQ: runbook-faq.md
      - Glossary: glossary.md
      - Contributing: contributing.md

# Internal planning docs stay in the repo (version-controlled) but are NOT
# published to the public site. ADRs (decision records) ARE published.
exclude_docs: |
  progress.md
  post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md
  post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md
  compliance-posture.md

validation:
  omitted_files: ignore
  absolute_links: ignore
  unrecognized_links: ignore
```
