  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/mcp-setup.md",
  "content": "# AI assistants (MCP setup)\n\nDataQ ships a built-in [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server so AI assistants — Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, VS Code / GitHub Copilot, Cursor — can answer questions like *\"what failed today?\"* or *\"run the orders suite\"* against your live DataQ instance, with the same per-suite permissions as the signed-in user.\n\n## Endpoint & authentication\n\nThe server is mounted on the deployed app at:\n\n```text\nhttps://<your-dataq-host>/mcp/\n```\n\n!!! warning \"Keep the trailing slash\"\n    `/mcp` answers with a **307 redirect** to `/mcp/`, and some HTTP clients drop the\n    `Authorization` header when following redirects — which then surfaces as a\n    confusing 401. Always configure clients with the `/mcp/` form.\n\nThe endpoint is **Azure AD–protected**: present the same bearer token the web UI uses (validated against the same tenant / audience / scope). Without auth configured, the endpoint is only mounted in local dev-bypass mode — never unauthenticated in a deployed environment (ADR [0008](adr/0008-mcp-server.md)).\n\n### Getting a token\n\nSign in to the DataQ web app, open your browser's developer tools → **Application → Session Storage** → the `oidc.user:…` entry → copy the `access_token` value.\n\n!!! note \"Tokens expire after ~1 hour\"\n    The pasted token is short-lived; when the client starts getting 401s, paste a\n    fresh one and restart the MCP server/connection. Long-lived DataQ-issued API\n    keys for headless MCP configs are tracked in ADR 0026\n    ([#461](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/461)).\n\n!!! danger \"Never commit a config that carries a token\"\n    Keep token-bearing MCP config files out of version control (in the DataQ repo\n    itself, `.gitignore` already covers `.vscode/*`).\n\n## Client configuration\n\n**Claude Desktop / Claude.ai** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) — and **GitHub Copilot** (`mcp.json`):\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"dataq\": {\n      \"url\": \"https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp/\",\n      \"headers\": { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer <AZURE_AD_ACCESS_TOKEN>\" }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**VS Code** (workspace `.vscode/mcp.json`, used by Copilot agent mode) uses a `servers` key — not `mcpServers` — plus an explicit `type`:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"servers\": {\n    \"dataq\": {\n      \"type\": \"http\",\n      \"url\": \"https://<your-dataq-host>/mcp/\",\n      \"headers\": { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer <AZURE_AD_ACCESS_TOKEN>\" }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nStart it via ++cmd+shift+p++ → **MCP: List Servers** → *dataq* → Start (or open Copilot Chat in agent mode — configured servers start on demand).\n\n**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) uses the same `mcpServers` shape as Claude Desktop.\n\n## The 8 tools\n\nEach tool is a thin wrapper over the same service layer as the REST API — per-suite authorization and failing-sample redaction apply identically.\n\n| Tool | What it answers |\n|---|---|\n| `list_suites` | \"What suites can I see?\" — id, datasource, env, check count, last run |\n| `get_suite_results` | \"What failed in suite X?\" — latest run's per-check outcomes |\n| `get_health_score` | \"How healthy is data quality overall?\" — score, pass rate, trend |\n| `get_adf_pipeline_status` | \"Why did pipeline Y fail?\" — recent orchestrator runs + correlated DQ run |\n| `trigger_suite_run` | \"Run the orders suite\" — dispatches a run, returns the run id |\n| `get_run_status` | \"Is it done?\" — live status + per-check progress |\n| `create_check` | \"Add a null check on email\" — authors a check on a suite you can edit |\n| `profile_column` | \"Profile the qty column\" — live null/distinct/min/max/top-values stats |\n\nTry these natural-language queries once connected:\n\n1. *\"What data quality checks failed today?\"*\n2. *\"Run the Retail Orders suite.\"* … *\"Is it done?\"*\n3. *\"Why did the ADF pipeline fail?\"*\n4. *\"Add a not-null check on order_number in the Retail Orders suite.\"*\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Cause / fix |\n|---|---|\n| 401 on every request | Token expired (~1 h) → paste a fresh one. Or the client followed the `/mcp` → `/mcp/` redirect and dropped the header → use `/mcp/` directly. |\n| 307 responses | Missing trailing slash — configure `/mcp/`. |\n| Server absent / connection refused locally | In a deployed environment the MCP server is unmounted unless Azure auth is configured (fail-closed by design). |\n| Tool call returns \"not found\" for a suite you can see in the UI as someone else | MCP calls run as the token's user — suite access is per-user, same as the web app. |\n"
}
```

30	  warehouse/file data.
31	- Let a harness pipeline (ADF or Airflow) succeed → the bound suite auto-runs and
32	  correlates on **Results → Pipelines**.
33	- Force a failing run → the Teams/Slack/email alert arrives with the right severity;
34	  a repeat failure is deduped.
35	- MCP: point Claude Desktop at `https://<frontend-host>/mcp` and run the 4 canonical
36	  queries (what failed today / run suite X / why did pipeline Y fail / add a null check).
37	
38	## Known limitations (v1)
39	
40	- **GX-only** check engine (Databricks DQX deferred to v1.1); batch-oriented (not
41	  streaming).
42	- **Single tenant**, suite-level access sharing; workspace-admin is a config allowlist.
43	- Interactive **datasource browsing** (container browser, 3-level UC catalog picker) is
44	  deferred — you specify targets explicitly. JSON flat files deferred (CSV/Parquet in v1).
45	- Auth is **Azure AD only** (no API keys / service tokens yet — see ADR 0026 / #461).
46	
47	## FAQ
48	
49	**Is ADF/Airflow a datasource?** No — they're orchestration providers DataQ monitors and
50	can trigger from. You never write checks against them. See **[Concepts](concepts.md)**.
51	
52	**Do I need Azure to run it locally?** No — local dev uses a dev-bypass auth and
53	docker-compose. Azure is one deployment target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013).
54	
55	**Where do failed-row samples go?** Stored with the result, **PII-redacted**, and purged
56	after a retention window — never written to logs.
57	
58	**Can an AI assistant use DataQ?** Yes — 8 MCP tools at `/mcp` (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai
59	/ Copilot / Cursor), Azure-AD authenticated. See the README's MCP section.

Rotation persists before the probe, so a bad new credential surfaces as 502 `connection_test_failed`; a store-write failure is 502 `connection_secret_write_failed` with the old credential untouched. 6 TestClient tests (rotate+verify ok, failed-verify-but-rotation-persists, write-fail 502, 404, secret-required 422). Type-agnostic — applies to all six connection types

149	### Column profiler (3 tasks — 3/3 ✅)
150	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Snowflake) — nulls, distinct count, min / max, top values — `profile_service` + `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (require_permission **edit**, suite-scoped so the connection is access-gated). Reads-only, persists nothing: one aggregate query (row count + null/distinct/min/max per column) + one top-N-values query per column, then `assemble_profile`. **SQL-injection-safe** — queries are built with the **SQLAlchemy Core expression language** (`select`/`table`/`column`, dialect-quoted) so there's no raw-string SQL sink (no S608/B608/CodeQL `py/sql-injection`); identifiers are additionally allowlist-validated (`validate_identifier`, strict `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$`) as defence-in-depth + a clean early 422, and `top_n` is `int()`-coerced. v1 → 422: non-Snowflake type (dispatch generalises Week 5), bad identifier, no schema; execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). min/max/top-values NaN-sanitised. 28 tests (22 pure: identifier allowlist incl. injection strings, compiled-SQL builders, assembly, div-by-zero, NaN; 6 endpoint via fake conn: stats, injection-422, unsupported-type-422, 502, edit-gated, no-schema-422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 90% (live `_open_connection` is the deferred warehouse seam)
151	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (ADLS / S3) — same stats via Pandas on sampled file — extended `profile_service` into a type dispatcher (`profile_connection`): SQL types → in-warehouse aggregation (unchanged), flat-file types (`adls_gen2`/`s3`) → download a **sample** of the file into Pandas and compute the same stats (`profile_dataframe`). Same `POST /suites/{id}/profile` endpoint, now polymorphic: SQL targets pass `table`/`schema`, flat-file targets pass `path` (+ optional `file_format`, else inferred from extension); response carries whichever identity applies. CSV + Parquet. **pandas "load less data" levers** (per the user's scale.html prompt): column projection (CSV `usecols`, Parquet `columns=` via pyarrow schema) so profiling 3 of N columns doesn't read all N, + row sampling (`_SAMPLE_ROWS`), + **zero-copy Arrow-backed dtypes** on the Parquet read (`dtype_backend="pyarrow"` — parquet is already Arrow, kept zero-copy; the stat helpers + `_to_native` are Arrow-scalar/`pd.NA`-safe). Stats are vectorised pandas (no Python row loops — enhancingperf N/A; CoW is a no-op for a read-only profiler + a process-global flag, so not toggled; pyarrow CSV engine rejected — it's incompatible with `nrows`/callable-`usecols`). NaN/Timestamp→JSON-safe. v1 → 422: unsupported type (UC still pending), missing target, unknown format, missing column; read failure → 502 (exception never echoed). Reuses `ColumnProfile`/`ProfileResult`. 24 new tests (pure `profile_dataframe`/`infer_file_format`/`_to_native`/projection-parse + endpoint via fake `_read_dataframe`); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 85% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). _Deferred: streaming/range reads (whole object still downloaded before sampling) + out-of-core (Dask) — future work if profiling cost bites._
152	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Unity Catalog) — via Databricks SQL Warehouse — added `unity_catalog` to the profiler's **SQL** branch (reuses `profile_table` + the SQLAlchemy Core query builders + `assemble_profile` — no duplicate aggregation logic). `_open_connection` now dispatches the engine by type (`_engine_args`): Snowflake URL or a `REDACTED` URL via the installed `databricks` SQLAlchemy dialect. UC's **3-level namespace** (`catalog.schema.table`) is handled by building the table with a `quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)` so the dialect emits three dotted parts rather than quoting the dotted string as one — verified by compiling the real builders against the Databricks dialect. Injection-safe: every part (catalog/schema/table/column) is allowlist-validated (no raw-string SQL, no CodeQL py/sql-injection surface). Endpoint gained `catalog` (request + response); the dispatcher requires it for UC (`422 profile_target_invalid` if absent). 12 new tests (catalog-aware builders compiled to SQL, `_engine_args` URL dispatch, UC endpoint stats via the same fake conn, missing-catalog 422, bad-catalog-identifier 422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 86% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). **Completes the column profiler across all 4 datasources.**

Extracted the shared GX machinery — snake_case→GX-class translation, GX-result→`SuiteOutcome` mapping, and the suite/validation-definition `run_expectations` flow — into `datasources/gx_runner.py` (reused by the Snowflake runner and the future UC runner; no duplication). Flat-file IO (`download_bytes` + full-file `read_dataframe`) moved to `flatfile.py` behind primitives (raw config + resolved secret, not the ORM — matches `build_snowflake_runner`), and the column profiler now shares it. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is fully unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution, not mocked) — only the network download is the deferred-smoke seam. 16 new tests; `gx_runner` 100%, `flatfile` 76% (only `download_bytes` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch (Snowflake vs flat-file) is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring; **freshness-by-filename** is the reserved `freshness` monitor kind (deferred, ADR 0012), not a GX expectation._
156	- [x] ✅ Batch resolution — resolve batching regex to matched files, pick latest or specific batch — `resolve_batch` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): a batch `pattern` is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest` selects the greatest key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort chronologically), falling back to the storage modified-time when the pattern has no group; `specific` selects the file whose key equals a given `batch`. `BatchNotFoundError` on no match / unknown batch. The filter+select logic is pure and fully unit-tested (8 tests); object listing (`list_files` — S3 `list_objects_v2` paginated / ADLS `list_blobs`) is the live seam, and `resolve_batch_file` composes list+resolve. _Wiring a check's target to a resolved batch path is the Week-5 `run_suite` dispatch._

New Celery-beat tick `dispatch_due_schedules` (60s) scans `enabled, next_run_at<=now` with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (no double-fire across overlapping ticks), resolves the suite target up front (invalid → skip + advance, never a queued→failed run), queues a `Run` (`triggered_by=schedule:<id>`) + dispatches via the shared `run_dispatch` (broker-fail → `mark_dispatch_failed` #227). `cron.validate_cron` probes a fire so an impossible-calendar cron (Feb 30 — `croniter.is_valid` passes it) is a clean 422, not a 500-on-create / crashed dispatcher tick; the dispatcher self-disables such a row instead of hot-looping. 37 tests (cron units incl. ## One-time provisioning

The datasource + compute infra is stood up by the external Terraform harness
(ADR 0021) — see `HARNESS_TODO.md`. Beyond that, this app needs:

1. An **ACA environment** + the three apps/job above (the backend image is on
   **GHCR**, not ACR — ADR 0023). The api/worker run `uvicorn …` / `celery …`;
   the migrate **job** runs `alembic upgrade head`. The `deploy/terraform/azure/` stack
---
   when it's non-empty). The api uses **internal ingress over HTTP** with
   `allow_insecure_connections = true` — ACA's internal service-to-service pattern; nginx
   must proxy as **HTTP/1.1** (`proxy_http_version 1.1`) or ACA ingress returns `426`.
   > **⚠️ One-time cutover cleanup — disable ACA EasyAuth on the api.** If the api was ever
   > **linked as an Azure Static Web App backend** (the pre-ADR-0028 topology), Azure
   > auto-enabled Container Apps **built-in authentication (EasyAuth)** on it with the
   > `azureStaticWebApps` identity provider. After the SWA→Container-App cutover the SWA is
   > destroyed but that EasyAuth config is **orphaned** and 401s *every* request at the
   > ingress (including `/healthz` and valid Bearer tokens), because DataQ does its **own**
   > token validation (`fastapi-azure-auth`) and doesn't use EasyAuth. Turn it off once:
   > ```
---
- Potential impact and severity assessment
- Any suggested mitigations

## Scope

Components in scope:
- FastAPI backend (`/api/v1/*`, `/mcp`)
- Azure AD authentication flow (MSAL token validation)
- Celery worker + GX execution path
- Key Vault secret access patterns

Out of scope:
- Vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies — report those upstream; we track them via Dependabot
- Issues requiring physical access to Azure infrastructure

- **Week 8 was badly under-reported** (1 ✅ / 9 🟡 / 19 ⬜): re-based against the actual test tree (79 backend + 47 frontend test files) it's **8 ✅ / 20 🟡 / 1 ⬜** — every 🟡 row now cites the exact test files covering it; the one real ⬜ is the `--cov-fail-under=80` CI gate, which is the week's exit-gate deliverable.
- **Open-issues bookkeeping**: 55 open verified via `gh` (5 Week-8 + 50 backlog, **zero** Week 1–7) — the register's Week-7 table (11 "open" issues, all actually closed) is retired; the snapshot row, Open-PRs row, and infra table (#92, governance-polish #8–#20) all corrected.
- **Aggregate re-tallied**: roadmap count went 146/188 (~78%) → **166 ✅ / 189 (~88%)**, with the counting conventions footnoted and verified by script against the real checkboxes.
- **Harness section**: retired `HARNESS_TODO.md` pointer → harness README, Flow B corrected to SQL-from-DAG + the AI sentiment stage (no notebook ever shipped), Free-Edition migration noted, and the **qa-verifier agent row flipped ✅** (#548).

**Other documents** (your follow-up ask) — swept README, CLAUDE.md, all docs-site pages, architecture.md, CONTRIBUTING, deploy/README, SECURITY.md, e2e READMEs, and post-v1-roadmap for the same classes of rot. Only three things surfaced, all fixed in the same PR: `deploy/README.md` pointed at the retired `HARNESS_TODO.md`; `.github/SECURITY.md` still scoped auth as "MSAL token validation" (MSAL is retired → OIDC + `fastapi-azure-auth`); and CLAUDE.md §13's follow-ups line listed closed #348 as open and mis-bucketed #205/#352 (both Week-8-milestoned) — that last one caught by the review agent.     name: Backend — dependency audit (pip-audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install pip-audit
        run: pip install pip-audit==2.10.0

      - name: pip-audit (full runtime + test surface)
        # Synchronous CVE gate over the entire runtime + test dependency tree
        # (single source: requirements-dev.txt) + transitive deps, against the
        # PyPI/OSV advisory DB. Complements the Dependabot alerts (full graph,
        # async) with a fail-fast merge check.
        #
        # The 5 ignored advisories are cryptography + pyOpenSSL CVEs blocked by
        # snowflake-connector-python<4 / snowflake-sqlalchemy<4 — a deliberate
        # major datasource bump tracked in #129 (the deadline for removing these).
    name: Frontend — dependency audit (pnpm audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
        with:
          version: 9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: pnpm audit (high+)
```

```
        # major datasource bump tracked in #129 (the deadline for removing these).
        #
        # Bounded retry: pip-audit resolves the requirements file via PyPI's
        # per-package JSON endpoint, so a single transient PyPI/OSV 5xx (e.g.
        # "503 Backend is unhealthy") aborts the whole audit and flakes the gate.
        # Retrying with backoff absorbs that *without* masking real findings — a
        # genuine CVE fails every attempt and still blocks (90s worst-case backoff).
        run: |
          audit() {
            pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt \
              --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-36 \
              --ignore-vuln PYSEC-2026-35 \
              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-26007 \
              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27448 \
              --ignore-vuln CVE-2026-27459
          }
      - name: pnpm audit (high+)
        # Fails on high/critical advisories in the dependency tree; lower
        # severities are reported but don't block (avoid noise from unfixable
        # transitive dev-tool advisories). Pairs with Dependabot alerts (async).
        run: pnpm audit --audit-level=high

  # ── CodeQL SAST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  codeql:

Keep me very Honest - How confident are you with this tool as data quality monitoring product as of current state

> AGENT

Honest, calibrated, no flattery:

**As an engineering artifact: high confidence. As a competitive data-quality *product*: maybe 4/10 today.** It's a genuinely well-built v1 skeleton of a DQ platform — but what exists is the part of the category that's table stakes, and the part that makes DQ products valuable is still on the post-v1 roadmap. The repo's own docs quietly admit this (§5: freshness/volume/anomaly "is the leap from 'GX runner' to DQ platform").

**What I'd defend without hesitation:**
- **It works as built, and that's verified, not claimed.** Four datasource paths run green against live infrastructure; orchestration-triggered checks are proven end-to-end (ADF failure visible in 4m14s; trigger-on-success firing real suites off real pipeline runs). Trigger-on-pipeline-success is a real differentiator over cron-only checkers.
- **The expensive-to-retrofit decisions are already right**: monitor-kind seam, adapter/runner registries, `ResultPublisher`, provider-agnostic infra. Adding capability later won't require rewrites — that's where most v1s fail.
- **Security/PII posture is well above v1 norm**: logger-level + column-aware sample redaction, tested authz matrix, fail-closed MCP, real incident-driven hardening (beat crash, stuck-run reaper, traceback leak). The alerting isn't naive spam — dedup, snooze, severity routing.
- MCP integration is ahead of the market curve, and it's genuinely tested.

**Where I'd stop you from overclaiming:**

1. **It monitors what you remember to check.** v1 is hand-authored expectations per table. The category leaders' (Monte Carlo, Anomalo) entire pitch is the inverse: automatic coverage — anomaly baselines, schema drift, ML freshness — with zero config. We pulled freshness/volume forward, which helps, but there's no anomaly detection, no auto-suggested checks, no schema-drift monitor. An unknown-unknown incident sails straight past DataQ.
2. **Scale is unproven and structurally weak on two of four paths.** The flat-file and UC runners load the whole file/table into pandas in the worker. The largest table this product has ever validated is a few thousand rows of synthetic retail data. A 100M-row table would OOM the worker, and there's no sampling/partition/incremental strategy for checks. The Snowflake path pushes down via SQL and is fine; the others are demo-scale.
3. **Every "verified" is self-referential.** One operator, one week of live running, against a harness designed by the same author. Zero exposure to real-world data pathology at scale — schema churn, half-written files mid-load, encoding chaos in volume. The adversarial unit battery is good; production battle-testing is effectively nil.
4. **No incident workflow, no lineage, no ownership.** Real DQ products live on "check failed → what's impacted downstream → who owns it → when was it resolved." DataQ has runs and alerts — no incident objects, no lineage, no resolution tracking, no data-access audit trail (#431 is flagged in our own compliance notes as the HIPAA gate).
5. **Single-tenant with a config-file admin list** — fine as an internal tool, not sellable. And the ecosystem is 4 datasources vs the 30–50 a category product ships; notably it can't even check the Postgres it runs on.
6. **The engine is a pinned, drifting third party.** GX Core's v1 API instability is documented in our own rules; the product's core capability rides on it.

**The honest one-liner:** today DataQ is a well-engineered, security-conscious *"Great Expectations as a service with orchestration awareness"* — credible as a single-team internal tool and a strong portfolio piece, roughly at the level of a good open-source Elementary/Soda-lite, and not yet in the conversation with commercial DQ platforms. Confidence it does what it's configured to do: ~8/10. Confidence a data team should pick it over existing options today: ~3/10. Confidence the architecture can get there if Theme A (auto-monitors), scale-aware runners, and lineage/incidents get built: ~7/10 — the foundations are the right ones, which is precisely what an 8-week v1 should have optimized for.
